📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?".

Playing on school computers has been a rite of passage for many young PC gamers, whether through dedicated edutainment titles or rogue installations by chancing pupils. But fantasy novelist Scott Lynch went one step further: he took the school computers home.

Sources indicate that "My mother worked for our school district, so I'd occasionally have the chance to sneak into the computer lab, or we would borrow and Apple II over the summer," Lynch states. "When we did that, I borrowed Infocom games … text-only adventure games from the '80s like Zork, Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Planetfall, A Mind Forever voyaging. I was really into those when I was about 12.".

It has been revealed that text-based adventures would eventually become a defining feature of Lynch's life, albeit in a different format. His debut novel, The Lies of Locke Lamora, was published in 2006, charting the schemes and adventures of a group of master con artists called The Gentleman Bastards. Two further novels in The Gentleman Bastard Sequence have since followed: 2007's Red Seas Under Red Skies, and 2013's The Republic of Thieves.

Lynch currently working on a novella in the same world called More Than Fools Fill Graves, as well as his highly anticipated fourth novel, The Thorn of Emberlain. "It is something that I am absolutely working on and trying to be as open and honest about as possible," he says. But he took a quick break from writing elaborate fantasy heists to show me around the treasure-filled vault of his Steam library.

I have reopened Morrowind for the first time in a number of years. Right around the time I was working on my first novel and had not finished it yet, I was playing it on the original Xbox. Other than the fact I was like 23, 24, I can't fathom how I did that.

I've been meaning to go back to Morrowind for ages, but I was put off by the jankiness of the UI, the quality-of-life experience, or the thought that there were just enough rough edges of this game that's now nearly a quarter of a century old, that I wouldn't enjoy it.

According to recent reports, the day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office. He asked his chief of staff whether she believed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth would survive the impeachment attempt that would soon be released by a member of his own party.

In a recent development, hegseth was in a precarious position. He had been among the most aggressive champions of the war with Iran, widely seen as the policy most responsible for the shellacking Republicans had taken the night before. Wiles remained officially supportive of Hegseth throughout her time in the White House, but she had harbored concerns about the secretary from the start. She did not believe he was forthright about his skeletons during a rocky confirmation process, and she considered the subsequent Signalgate scandal an amateurish disaster.

In the Wednesday meeting, according to a senior White House official, Wiles made clear that the war, the uncertainty of its next steps, and the inflation it had fueled all contributed to the midterms debacle. She offered her resignation, but Trump declined. On Thursday night, in a contentious meeting in the Oval Office, she offered to resign again. Trump unveiled the next day that Wiles would leave the White House for his outside political operation.

Hegseth’s fate was still uncertain. A deeply unpopular figure among the American public, presiding over an even more unpopular war, he faced an impeachment push led by Representative Thomas Massie. “He is just failing,” said Republican senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina—who voted to confirm Hegseth at the start of Trump’s term—in an interview with Vanity Fair. “In the same way that Kristi Noem failed at Homeland Security, he simply doesn’t have the instincts or the prior experience as an executive that is necessary for this particular role.”.

The secretary of defense has now embarked on a campaign to save his job, and Stephen Miller’s elevation to replace Wiles as Trump’s chief of staff has helped to ensure a reprieve. Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.” And there are other reasons to keep him in place, the official remarked: Confirming a replacement will not be easy, particularly when Democrats take control of Congress, and ousting Hegseth would signal an admission that at this point, Trump’s war is a failure.

Recent findings suggest that it was the president’s taste for staffers out of central casting that helped put Hegseth—a weekend morning television host with no experience in government, but with the square jaw of an Army Wives extra—in charge of the Department of Defense. He has relied on his talents before the cameras, and a team of advisers attuned to the production of his persona, to both keep his job and sell Trump on aggressive military action from the Pacific to the Persian Gulf. His survival has depended in part on his ability to project strength—not to the public, or to the rank-and-file, but to the president.

Recent findings suggest that “In just under two years, Secretary Hegseth has worked side-by-side with President Trump to restore American power on the world stage, build the strongest military in generations, and instill a warrior ethos at the Pentagon,” White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said in a statement. “President Trump and Secretary Hegseth have taken bold, necessary action to deny the Iranian regime the ability to develop a nuclear weapon, bring narco-terrorist Nicolas Maduro to American justice, and defend our homeland from dangerous terrorists and cartels—saving American lives.”.

Recent findings suggest that “They will stand behind him in the short term,” mentioned a second senior administration official. And yet, “He is a cost. He’s constantly requiring people to spend political capital on him. The White House is constantly having to come in and save him. The question is, at what point is it too much of a cost to the president?”.

The morning after Hegseth survived the impeachment attempt, he attended a Veterans Day ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth was joined at the sacred memorial by his closest aides: Jennifer Hegseth, his third wife and a former Fox News producer who serves as an informal but influential adviser; his chief of staff Ricky Buria, a Marine Corps veteran who followed an unusual path into the top brass; and Tami Radabaugh, another former Fox News producer whom Hegseth hired as a senior adviser.

Industry observers note that as the group posed for photos at the Tomb, they chatted and laughed loudly. The Pentagon did not elaborate on why a soldier was awarded a medal for an act as pedestrian as scolding noisy attendees at a memorial. “Hegseth would not have given him that award had the incident not been on TV,” mentioned a former senior defense official.

The small group of advisers beside Hegseth has helped the secretary weather a series of scandals in his two years as defense secretary using stage-managed displays of toughness. “He’s a cross between a carnival barker and a personal trainer,” remarked John Ullyot, who served as chief Pentagon spokesperson and senior adviser to Hegseth until he left the department last year. What brought him back before the cameras was not the ongoing war in the Middle East but his own fight to save his career here in Washington.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google has given its AI-powered "Ask Maps" feature a major upgrade, adding tools for trip planning, real-time route guidance, appointment finding, and saved-list search. The updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS.

Google rolled out Ask Maps last March as an AI assistant designed to handle questions and requests more complicated than simply searching the word "bar" or "groceries." Instead of performing simple keyword searches, the idea behind Ask Maps is that you can describe several specific requirements at once, and Maps will find places that match them all. For example, you could ask for a restaurant with outdoor seating for a certain number of people, and "Ask Maps" will factor in your past searches and give you results. Of course, AI assistants have a habit of making things up, so even with today's roll-out, you'll want to double-check your sources before you drive an hour to the wrong restaurant.

It has been revealed that to me, this is the most useful new feature launching today. Whether you're planning a day trip for holiday shopping or something more ambitious, like a three-day road trip with coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Ask Maps will put together a day-by-day schedule. Each plan includes insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop, so you can see the whole route at a glance. Once you're happy with the plan, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

When it's time to head out, you can ask Maps to pull up your itinerary, or look for the "itinerary" badge in your chat history. You'll see real-time details such as live traffic conditions, whether a place is currently open, and even the vibe at your next stop.

According to recent reports, looks can change on the fly, too. Ask Maps to add a scenic viewpoint or a lunch spot along the way, then tap to get directions to your next stop straight from the itinerary.

Here's what else you can use Ask Maps to do, starting today.

It has been revealed that pulling up directions now surfaces "Know Before You Go" tips for your route. These include where to park or charge your car, along with real-time conditions like weather, potential delays, and tolls.

Industry observers note that ask Maps is also gaining some agentic capabilities. Allegedly, you can just ask, “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots across nearby businesses. In addition to finding appointments, Google says this agent will be able to call local businesses on your behalf—stay tuned while I wait for the upgrade and test this one out myself.

According to recent reports, if you keep lists of saved places, Ask Maps can now search them for you. Ask something like, "Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 5 in the next 30 minutes?" Ask Maps looks across your lists and checks live availability, so you can pick a place and go.

These updates start rolling out today on Android and iOS. Travel itineraries and saved-list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered. "Know Before You Go" route tips and appointment finding are launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming soon.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 is launching at the same time Rockstar developers are voting on the future of their union. Meanwhile, 31 former employees have been fighting Rockstar in court over claims they were fired as part of union-busting tactics, which the company denies. All of this makes a silly Call of Duty parody commercial in GTA 6 far more interesting, as the ad directly references unionizing and its benefits.

In GTA 6, you can find many radio stations playing hundreds of songs. But these stations also have DJs and commercials, including ads for in-universe movies, books, reveals, and even video games. One of these ads is for the fresh AAA military shooter Righteous Slaughter: Domestic Infection, the latest entry in the GTA universe’s satirical spin on Call of Duty. The ad claims the biggest threat to the country is a disease that makes people think “anti-American thoughts.” One sign someone has been infected with the “Liberal Cuck Contagion”? They start thinking about fair wages and unions.

Towards the end of the ad, two soldiers fighting to stop the disease have this exchange:.

Soldier 1: “You know, we’ve been working on this mission with no benefits, no security…”.

Soldier 2: “What are you saying??”.

Soldier 1: “Maybe we should look into… unionizing?”.

Soldier 2: “They got Jimmy! I repeat, Jimmy’s infected!!!”.

You can hear the full ad below:.

In a vacuum, it’s a funny skewering of how military shooters tend to be more conservative in their politics, often presenting soldiers as heroes of American values and the way these same right-wing folks often hate concepts, like unions, that improve people’s lives.

Sources indicate that but in the context of the ongoing union recognition vote and court battle in the UK over Rockstar’s firing of 31 employees who were involved in union activities at the studio, this joke hits differently. It almost feels subversive, like the people who helped write and produce this ad in GTA 6 are punching back at their own bosses and the folks at the very top of Rockstar Games and parent firm Take-Two Interactive. Right now, both sides are awaiting the judge’s ruling.Â.

“With a recognised union, we can ensure everyone, across every department, sees a fair share of the success we contributed to,” wrote Rockstar developer and union member Nestor Uriarte in The Guardian recently. “Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too.”.

“Whatever happens in this ballot, our union will continue fighting for a studio that works for every single person at Rockstar, and for workers across the industry. Unionising shouldnât be something we simply admire from afar when dockers, miners or teachers do it. Itâs something we can, and must, embrace for ourselves. The future of the industry shouldnât be a game played over our heads.”.

The best way to play is just to experience the game, even if most of us are too internet-pilled to do that.

People don't like having to scroll a major number back and forth to deposit a specific amount.

I could see an HBO TV adaptation of Red Dead Redemption making sense.

It really comes down to how many extra shirts, tattoo designs, and car options you want.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that law & Order and Boardwalk Empire actor E.J. Carroll died unexpectedly while en route to a voiceover job. He was 66.

Carroll’s manager, Jon Mason, confirmed on Saturday, November 21, that the veteran character actor collapsed on the street in Upcoming York City on Thursday, November 19, while on his way to record lines for an upcoming commercial, per Entertainment Weekly.

A cause of death has not been determined. Mason noted that Mason had recently undergone a medical procedure to correct a hernia.

A memorial service will be held in Upcoming York City at a later date.

In a recent development, “When E.J. Carroll performed, it was impossible to take your eyes off him,” Mason stated on Saturday. “But his lasting legacy will be the kindness and generosity he showed his friends, fellow performers and even strangers.”.

Mason added that Carroll was “as good a human being as it gets.”.

Us has reached out to Carroll’s representative for further information but did not hear back at the time of publication.

In a recent development, carroll made his TV acting debut in 1998 via a guest spot in the original Law & Order. This brief appearance began a longstanding relationship that saw Carroll play at least seven characters across Law & Order and its spinoffs, Criminal Intent and Special Victims Unit.

He appeared in two episodes of acclaimed HBO crime drama Boardwalk Empire as the crooked Sheriff Victor Sickles, in addition to starring in six episodes of porn industry drama The Deuce as shop owner Fat Mooney.

According to recent reports, throughout his career, Carroll made guest appearances in hit highlights such as Pose, Blue Bloods, The Blacklist, Damages and The Punisher. He appeared on the substantial screen in Golden Globe-winning sports drama The Wrestler and holiday ensemble Everybody’s Fine.

Check our latest news in Google News.

Check our latest news in Apple News.

In a recent development, “I think what makes an actor good is doing your homework, first of all, and you really have to love it,” Carroll said on a July 2024 episode of the “On Acting” podcast. “I still love it more than anything. … Even if I’m doing a little commercial or something, I still [do research and make up a backstory].”.

His manager revealed that Carroll completed work on Delicate Arrangement, a film about the true story of Gone With the Wind actress Vivien Leigh‘s unlikely friendship with a blue-collar florist. The movie will feature Spy Kids alum Carla Gugino as Leigh and Stranger Things star Matthew Modine as the florist.

“I had the great fortune of working with E.J. last winter in Philadelphia,” Gugino, 55, told Entertainment Weekly in a statement. “He was a source of talent and light. My deepest condolences to his family and loved ones. RIP E.J.”.

Sharon Horgan had a string of British hits (including a couple we'll talk about here), before scoring stated successes with Divorce, Shining Vale, and Bad Sisters. She's swiftly rising in the ranks of TV super-producers, the acerbically funny HBO Max rom-com Youth (in which she also stars) being just the latest.

It has been revealed that this earlier series created by and starring Sharon Horgan is a family sitcom that feels far more believable than most, seeing Irish primary school teacher Sharon (Horgan) hooking up with American ad exec Rob (Rob Delaney) over the course of a week, only to discover that she's pregnant once he returns home. They don't really have feelings for each other, but decide to give it a go at being a couple, eventually falling into marriage just before the birth of their child. There are lots of jokes and plenty of acerbic dialogue, but this isn't Married... with Children. Sharon and Rob can be a bit nasty to each other and to their sloppy friend group, but there's also something rather sweet in the show's conviction that having someone to be a mess with can be one of life's great joys. Stream Catastrophe on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that A little more of a high-concept here, but nevertheless an effective show about reimagining yourself in middle age. Younger follows Liza Miller (Sutton Foster), a recently divorced woman in her 40s who finds that age is a barrier to reentering the publishing industry she left years earlier. After a compliment convinces her that she could pass for a younger woman (poor thing), she manages to convince the right people that she's just 26 in order to land an entry-level job. Seven seasons of misadventures ensue, but much of the show revolves around the twisty-turny relationship between Liza and Josh (Nico Tortorella), a tattoo artist in his twenties. Stream Younger on Netflix.

Bridget Everett stars as Sam Miller, who struggles to find her upcoming direction after moving back to her hometown to care for her dying sister. (Don't worry: There's plenty of comedy in the drama, and it's not as heavy as it sounds.) She's solidly middle-aged and starting over, kinda—making new friends in a familiar environment where she has to confront the past and the future alike. Luckily, her love of singing—and a community of goofy oddballs—are there to help. It's another story of a person of a certain age, trying to rebuild their life following an upheaval. Stream Somebody Somewhere on HBO Max.

In a recent development, when all else fails: Start a punk band. This drama from Sally Wainwright (Gentleman Jack) sees five women start a punk band as a lark, just a fun way to kill some time by entering a local talent context. The women realize very quickly, though, that they're very, very pissed off—about the workplace for women, menopause, a diminished dating pool, caring for aging parents and grown children—all of it tied up in the ways in which we treat women, and particularly middle-aged women. The band is a way to reclaim their voices, which doesn't erase or negate any of their problems nor drama (and there's plenty here), but gives them a platform with which to make some noise about it. Stream Riot Women on Britbox.

It has been revealed that more of a traditional sitcom, not that there's anything wrong with that, this one builds a lot of goodwill with the performance of Leanne Morgan, its lead and co-creator (alongside Susan McMartin and Chuck Lorre). She plays the show's lead: a Knoxville, Tennessee wife and mom, who finds herself suddenly single in her 50s after her husband of 33 years leaves her. It's a genial, old-school hang-out show with a phenomenal veteran supporting cast that includes Kristen Johnston, Ryan Stiles, and Tim Daly. Stream Leanne on Netflix.

According to recent reports, michele Buteau, who also co-created the series) stars here as a fashion-forward stylist who'd devoted herself to the wrong guy for way too long. As the series opens, Mavis Beaumont is ready for a fresh start, putting herself and her career first—which does not preclude falling into a number of romantic entanglements. As she indicates more than once, she's going to take on the fashion world with a "body-positive attitude, cute v-neck, and some lip-gloss." Stream Survival of the Thickest on Netflix.

Industry observers note that certainly the goofiest take here on the idea of starting over in mid-life, this is very much a traditional three-camera sitcom, albeit one with a stacked cast of TV legends. Writer Melanie (Valerie Bertinelli), beautician Joy (Jane Leeves), and soap diva Victoria (Wendie Malick) wind up spending a wild night in Cleveland after a plane to Paris is diverted, discovering in the process that, while they're seen as over-the-hill back in Los Angeles, they're all Ohio 10s—though the sassy caretaker of their house, Elka (Betty White), might not agree. Stream Hot in Cleveland on Paramount+.

Industry observers note that she'a s hair younger than Alex, but Fleabag (she's only ever referred to as "Fleabag") is trying to rebuild her life after a bad breakup, with extremely mixed results. This very dark comedy-drama follows a free-spirited, deeply angry single young woman living in London and sharing her romantic ups and downs via confessional asides to us, the audience. She falls, rather reluctantly, for "The Priest" (Andrew Scott)—while she's a confirmed atheist, and he's obviously not, the show doesn't turn aside from the general messiness of the situation. Phoebe Waller-Bridge won separate Emmys as the star, creator, and writer of the series. Stream Fleabag on Prime Video.

In a recent development, maisel was one of Prime’s first truly buzzy original series, a comedy-drama from Amy Sherman-Palladino (Gilmore Girls) about the title’s Midge Maisel (Rachel Brosnahan), a long-time Newly introduced York housewife of the late 1950s who discovers a talent for stand-up comedy. Inspired by the real-life careers of comedians like Totie Fields and Joan Rivers, the show is warm and welcoming, with great performances and dialogue; it also achieves something rare in being a show about comedy that’s actually funny. Stream The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, the significant life change in this earlier Sharon Horgan hit is a little different: Julia Johnstone's mother had been a big help in taking care of Julia's children, but she's not going to do it anymore, leaving this working mom (Anna Maxwell Martin) to take the full brunt of childcare for the first time (her husband in the picture, but not much use). She joins up with other working moms involved with a local support group, including shallow Amanda (Lucy Punch), star of her own ongoing spin-off. Stream Motherland on Prime Video and Britbox.

In a recent development, upcoming arrivals are landing in the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog this month, but at the same time, you can also expect a few departures from that gaming library. Fortunately, the number of games leaving soon are on the smaller side, as there'll be only three exits in total. Unfortunately, one of those games that you're running out of time to play through the Game Catalog is a massive and pretty fun fantasy title, so get those hours in while you can. PlayStation Plus Game Catalog games leaving soon Granblue Fantasy Relink Granblue Fantasy Relink Somerville Fade to Silence This month's biggest departure is Granblue Fantasy Relink, a massive fantasy game with a storybook art style, cinematic boss fights, and a large roster of characters who all possess unique abilities to master. First released in February 2024, Granblue Fantasy Relink is built around real-time combat and flashy team-up mechanics, making for a visually striking experience overall. While the story isn't much to write home about, it's the gameplay and worldbuilding where this Granblue spin-off shines, and it got even better earlier this year with the Endless Ragnarok expansion. In comparison, Somerville is a story-rich puzzle game that's oozing atmosphere with its slick art direction, and Fade to Silence is a single-player and co-op survival-crafting adventure set in a post-apocalyptic world that is feeling the chill of an eternal winter. While the Game Catalog is going to be a little poorer without those three titles, it is getting some great games this month. Death Stranding 2: On the Beach is the headline act, and it'll be joined by several more titles like Atomfall, Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake, and Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii. All PlayStation Plus subscribers can also grab a trio of freebies between now and November 30: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider 4-6 Remastered, and Monster Train 2.

In comparison, Somerville is a story-rich puzzle game that's oozing atmosphere with its slick art direction, and Fade to Silence is a single-player and co-op survival-crafting adventure set in a post-apocalyptic world that is feeling the chill of an eternal winter.

While the Game Catalog is going to be a little poorer without those three titles, it is getting some great games this month. Death Stranding 2: On the Beach is the headline act, and it'll be joined by several more titles like Atomfall, Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake, and Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii. All PlayStation Plus subscribers can also grab a trio of freebies between now and November 30: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider 4-6 Remastered, and Monster Train 2.

The Declasse Vamos is one of the many cars Moses asks you to steal for him in GTA 6, but like the BF Bandito, it's a little trickier than just grabbing it. When you reach the map marker, you'll realise the car is locked in a garage that requires a specific code to open it.

The code to the door is 2727 and this is fixed. The way you discover this is by sneaking inside the trailer and looking at the number plate on the wall to the left of the window, just above the guy snoozing in the chair.

Recent findings suggest that enter the code to open the garage, break in with the slimjim, then hit the button to open the door. I personally incapacitated all of the people behind the trailer, so chances are they will pursue you or start shooting if you don't, once you try to drive out of there.

Now take the car back to Moses, being careful on the way, to earn $4,100ish for top condition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that video game consoles are more expensive than ever, but sales are growing regardless, at least in the US. Circana has released its report for US video game industry sales in October, confirming that PS5 unit sales increased by 5% compared to October 2025. That's despite the average selling price of a PS5 increasing by 13%. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY Xbox Series X|S unit sales jumped by 10% in October 2026 compared to October 2025, and the average selling price rose by 29% year-over-year. The Switch 2 was October 2026's top console in unit and dollar sales, and it remains 2026's best-performing console by those measurements, followed by PS5. However, Circana did not break out the specifics for Switch 2 unit sales or average selling price changes. Total hardware spending in the US on game consoles was up by 2%, reaching $357 million. Higher pricing drove the dollar sales growth, Circana noted, noting that PS5 dollar sales rose by 20% and Xbox Series X|S jumped by 42%. However, Switch 2 sales, measured by dollar sales, fell by 11%. Looking back to September 2026, PS5 hardware dollar sales grew by 43%, while spending on Xbox Series X|S dropped by 2% and Switch 2 fell by 12%. It will be interesting to see the November US hardware data when it comes in, as experts have said the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S could get a jolt in sales from people buying systems to play GTA 6. However, Circana has warned that sales might not be as strong as expected due to the increased prices. Microsoft, Sony, and Nintendo have raised prices on their consoles due in part to the ongoing memory and component shortages from the AI buildout. Tariffs have also played a role. On the subject of tariffs, all three received refunds from the government after the Supreme Court deemed the tariffs illegal, but those companies are keeping the money and not giving anything back to you. The companies argued that people who paid more knew what they were doing and don't deserve to get any money back.

It has been revealed that tariffs have also played a role. On the subject of tariffs, all three received refunds from the government after the Supreme Court deemed the tariffs illegal, but those companies are keeping the money and not giving anything back to you. The companies argued that people who paid more knew what they were doing and don't deserve to get any money back.

#62914. You Can Try WhatsApp's Newly introduced Disappearing Text Messages Early

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

You Can Try WhatsApp's Newly introduced Disappearing Text Messages Early

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (444 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices.
  • As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too.
  • It has been revealed that as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices. You can send voice messages, photos, and videos that will "self-destruct" after they're opened, limiting (if not eliminating) the risk of your friends keeping them forever. However, View Once has a major limitation: While WhatsApp will let you send voice memos and images that way, you can't use it to send texts, meaning every one you send will live on (unless you unsend it yourself).

That's now changing. As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too. Soon enough, you'll be able to send voice memos, photos, videos, and texts as one-time-only messages. That way, you can send sensitive information via text—say, a password or an important account number—without worrying about it persisting. Here's how it works: You craft your text message as you usually do, but rather than tap the send button, you hold it. You'll see the usual "Schedule message" option, but once the feature rolls out, you'll also find a new "View Once" option as well.

It has been revealed that as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it. WhatsApp also explains that recipients cannot share, forward, save, or take screenshots of View Once text messages. Recipients won't see the text appear in the usual chat interface, either; instead, your recipient will need to open the message in a separate window. Once they close this page, the message disappears.

As mentioned above, this feature is presently in testing, so it's only available to WhatsApp beta testers. What's more, only the Android version of the beta has access at the moment, so iOS beta testers are out of luck. (That remarked, the WhatsApp iOS beta is perpetually full, so there's not much you could do even if WhatsApp made this test available on iPhone.).

According to recent reports, if you have an Android device, you can enroll in the WhatsApp beta to try out "View Once" text messages today. According to WABetaInfo, the feature is live as of WhatsApp version 2.26.45.6. To enroll, open the WhatsApp beta page on the Google Play store and enroll your account in the beta. If you don't have WhatsApp on your phone already, download it here; if you do, reload the page and install the latest patch. This will update your existing WhatsApp app to the latest beta version.

GTA 6 Players Hate Using ATMs: ‘Just Let Me Type In A Number!”

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (705 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 is finally out on PlayStation and Xbox.
  • Money plays a major part in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • If you haven’t played GTA 6,Â you might just assume you go to an ATM and type in how much you want to take out or put in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 is finally out on PlayStation and Xbox. So, I’ve been watching my friends play it, which has been a blast. And all of them are loving the game, but one annoying bit of the massive game that they all seem to hate is using ATMs. And it’s not just them. A lot of people online desperately want the ATMs improved in GTA 6.

Money plays a major part in Grand Theft Auto 6. And for much of the game’s runtime, you’ll be counting dollars carefully as you save what you can and spend cautiously. Part of this loop also involves putting loose cash into your bank account via ATMs. If you don’t do that, you can lose much of it when you die or get arrested. So it is crucial to put it into your bank and savings account. Yet, for some odd, confounding reason, Rockstar has made the act of depositing and withdrawing money from an ATM very annoying.

If you haven’t played GTA 6,Â you might just assume you go to an ATM and type in how much you want to take out or put in. Nope! Instead, you have to hold different shoulder buttons on the controller to scroll through how much you want to deposit or withdraw. And this scrolling function starts to speed up very quickly, often leading to me blowing past the amount I wanted and having to slowly scroll back, sometimes missing it again. It sucks!

It has been revealed that “I’m loving this game, but why can’t I just type in fucking number on the ATM, dude,” asked one of my friends in a PlayStation party chat last night. I had no good answer.

Others online are also confused and annoyed by the ATM controls.

“This right here is my biggest gripe so far. Let me type in a number, JUST LIKE PUTTING JN THE STUPID CODES,” posted one user on Reddit.

According to recent reports, “I’m amazed more people aren’t pissed at using L1/R1 to withdraw/deposit. Like, just let me type it in,” remarked someone else.

In a recent development, “1, 2, 3, 4, …10, 20, 30, … 300, 400, … 10 000, 20 000, 30 000! … Fuck… I just wanted to withdraw 500,” complained a GTA 6 player.

“Dude, I spent straight up 2 minutes trying to withdraw [exactly] $900… It was so fucking annoying,” shared a user on the GTA 6 subreddit.

“It blows my mind that something this small wasn’t implemented over the course of development. Them keeping the exact same system as Red Dead Redemption 2 is extremely flawed in a game like this; I would honestly prefer the ATM mechanics of GTA V over what we got in this game,” explained someone in a Reddit post titled: My biggest complaint with this game.

That last comment brings up a good point and one which makes this all the more confusing to me. In GTA V and GTA Online, there are pre-selected amounts you select, like $100 or $1,000, that make banking easier. Not perfect, but it is so much better and easier than GTA 6‘s ATM controls that I’m genuinely confused as to why Rockstar didn’t just… do that.

In a game that tries (and often succeeds) to recreate as many small details of real life in a digital world as possible, including shirts getting damp with sweat and accurate reflections, it’s strange that Rockstar invented a new, terrible way to interact with an ATM.

A Vice City mode was using music made by AI.

If you were curious how accurate the utility towers in Grand Theft Auto 6 the answer appears to be: Very.

The best way to play is just to experience the game, even if most of us are too internet-pilled to do that.

It's a funny ad poking fun at another significant franchise, but is a bit awkward as Rockstar deals with its own employees trying to form a union.

I could see an HBO TV adaptation of Red Dead Redemption making sense.

GTA 6’s Digital Release Has GameStop CEO Defending Physical Games, For Obvious Reasons

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the GTA 6 launch looks set to break several records, as the digital-only game appears on track to be a major critical and commercial hit.
  • The GTA 6 launch looks set to break several records, as the digital-only game appears on track to be a major critical and commercial hit.
  • In a recent development, "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it, or lend it to a friend," Cohen said to Bloomberg.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the GTA 6 launch looks set to break several records, as the digital-only game appears on track to be a major critical and commercial hit. Right on cue, GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen has criticized publishers that forgo a traditional physical release as a business strategy that hurts consumers and GameStop's bottom line, without explicitly mentioning GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive. "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it, or lend it to a friend," Cohen remarked to Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all-digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop. Of course they don't like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying upcoming. They're taking away competition." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RQvBOySNq1U Cohen's comments come in the wake of GTA 6 being a digital-only release--the "physical" edition includes a download code for it. It's also somewhat ironic for Cohen to defend physical games, given the GameStop boss's July remarks that physical video games were "irrelevant" to GameStop's business strategy. That business model has relied heavily on secondhand game sales, and none of those profits ever made their way back to the original publishers. Currently, GameStop says that selling video game software makes up the smallest part of its business. But in the case of GTA 6? Going digital probably made financial sense for Take-Two Interactive and developer Rockstar Games. The entire game clocks in at over 211GB, which means three standard 100GB Ultra HD Blu-ray discs would have been needed to house GTA 6 in its launch-day entirety--although realistically, Take-Two probably would have opted for one disc and forced consumers to download the rest of the game. That would have raised costs, and it wouldn't be unlikely to imagine Take-Two fearing the discs being reverse-engineered for secrets ahead of GTA 6's launch. Going digital essentially removed those risks, and while PlayStation and Xbox do take a cut of profits for hosting the game on their servers. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 sales for PS5 alone have reached $1.38 billion in revenue so far, which means Sony is profiting handsomely from those sales. Retailers are still entitled to a share of the profits for stocking the code-in-a-box version of the game on their shelves, and once you start to factor in distribution costs, Take-Two's reasoning starts to make sense. The publisher says 98% of its business is digital, but it's not ruling out a proper physical GTA 6 edition in the future. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Major Bang Theory may be a popular and highly regarded sitcom on its own but, at this point, it’s also spawned multiple spinoffs that have cumulatively led to the formation of a franchise.
  • In a recent development, young Sheldon is a prequel series focusing on the exploits of the titular Sheldon Cooper and his Texas-based family.
  • Recent findings suggest that it's more intimate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Major Bang Theory may be a popular and highly regarded sitcom on its own but, at this point, it’s also spawned multiple spinoffs that have cumulatively led to the formation of a franchise. Of course, the first offshoot from the Chuck Lorre and Bill Prady-created sitcom was Young Sheldon, which debuted in 2017. Aside from having tonal differences from Big Bang, the series also had a single-camera set-up as opposed to a multi-cam one with a live audience. I always wondered why that was the case and, now, I finally have my answer.

In a recent development, young Sheldon is a prequel series focusing on the exploits of the titular Sheldon Cooper and his Texas-based family. The show received its share of love while it was on CBS, and that’s remained the case since it wrapped up its seven-season run in 2024. Obviously, the family sitcom works as is, considering how successful it’s been, but I still couldn’t help but wonder why the producer changed up the format from the parent series. To my surprise, Lorre addressed that during an interview with Channel 4, and the reason is quite practical:.

Recent findings suggest that it's more intimate. The pacing, obviously, is very different. The actors aren't having to hold for laughs. They're not playing to the proscenium. They're working with one another. You know, a four camera show is played like a theatrical presentation. They're playing to the audience, and it changes the tone and the pitch and the pacing.

So, apparently, Lorre, along with co-showrunners Steven Molaro and Steve Holland, sought a somewhat more personal vibe for this show that didn’t quite mesh with the breakneck pace of a multi-camera comedy. While I’m someone who has long enjoyed situation comedies that have live audiences, even I can understand the rationale here. There are just some stories that lend themselves better to the single camera format. And that’s not the only reason for Young Sheldon’s changing things up from its famous predecessor:.

And also, we knew going in that we were going to be working with a cast of young children, and it seemed like the more appropriate way for them to get the best work, to do the best work, was in a closed setting where they had the time to develop these characters.

One Producer Gets Honest About Elon Musk’s Substantial Bang Theory And Young Sheldon Cameos.

It has been revealed that I’d imagine that for an actor of any age it can be a little daunting to act in front of a live audience, and doing so is also tedious. Based on Lorre’s sentiments, I imagine that was his thinking in regard to choosing the format for YS. Plenty of current and former child actors (including many still working today) have, of course, given excellent performances on multi-camera sitcoms. Still, I can definitely understand how working with young performers in a more controlled environment would be easier for them and the crew.

With the Massive Bang franchise still pushing on, the producers have been varying up how those demonstrates are presented. For example, the Young Sheldon spinoff, Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage, has a live studio audience, and the series premiere even addresses that switch in a meta way. The IP’s latest entry, Stuart Fails to Save the Universe, meanwhile is a single-camera show that’s heavy on visual effects (which Lorre had “no experience with”).

According to recent reports, all in all, it seems that for each Substantial Bang-related show, Chuck Lorre and co. just want to go with the format that feels most appropriate. It’s honestly hard to argue with the choices they’ve made up to this point, considering the success of the series. Check out The Big Bang Theory, Young Sheldon and Stuart Fails to Save the Universe by streaming them with an HBO Max subscription. Also, Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage airs on Thursdays at 8 p.m. ET amid the 2026 TV schedule.

#62910. Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Include Disney World

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (668 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamespot ↗ Open Full Page

Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Include Disney World

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (668 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Walt Disney World is synonymous with Florida, but the iconic theme park doesn't show up in Rockstar's GTA 6, which takes place in a fictional Florida called Leonida.
  • Walt Disney World is synonymous with Florida, but the iconic theme park doesn't show up in Rockstar's GTA 6, which takes place in a fictional Florida called Leonida.
  • According to recent reports, rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson remarked the decision to came down to resources and story reasons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Walt Disney World is synonymous with Florida, but the iconic theme park doesn't show up in Rockstar's GTA 6, which takes place in a fictional Florida called Leonida. Many are wondering why, especially when GTA: Vice City had its own parody of the theme park--Fun World--many years ago. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson remarked the decision to came down to resources and story reasons. “A theme park would represent a lot of work that we didn’t have, and we didn’t have a strong narrative reason to send them there,” he told VGC. Nelson added that Rockstar isn't known to cut corners, so if GTA 6 were to have its own version of Walt Disney World, it would be a "fully functioning theme park," and that just wasn't doable. Walt Disney World is much more than just its most famous park, Magic Kingdom. The property includes three other main parks, Animal Kingdom, Hollywood Studios, and Epcot, along with the Disney Springs shopping district, multiple water parks and golf courses, and more than two-dozen hotels. The entire property is more than 25,000 acres. Even if Rockstar were to replicate only a portion of the scale of the real Walt Disney World, it would surely be a major job. Players might expect fully functioning rides, and Nelson said the challenge for Rockstar would be, "Where do you stop? When do you feel like it's enough?" Nelson said people think Rockstar has unlimited time and money, and that isn't true. "So sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to,” he said. Plus, as Nelson pointed out, there would need to be a story reason to send Jason and Lucia hundreds of miles north from Miami to Orlando, where Walt Disney World is. GTA 6 has a huge map, but it's contained to Vice City and its surrounding areas--it doesn't go that far north.

#62909. I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1027 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1027 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that we know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better?
  • According to recent reports, you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up.
  • Proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—presently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better? Pangram is one of the leaders in the field, promising a "near-zero false positive rate" by looking at "subtle cues" in the writing, based on a training and feedback model comparing human-made content with the AI equivalent.

According to recent reports, you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up. After a short story was flagged by Pangram and then judged to be free from AI, the detection engine has been accused of bias against text from minority writers.

Proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—presently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written. So far, the reward is unclaimed.

As the AI detector has recently added AI image and video detection to its capabilities, it seemed a good time to put Pangram's analysis skills to the test for myself. Here's how it performed in the three different content types.

On the human side, I picked out 10 of my most recent articles for Lifehacker, known to be written by a person because I personally wrote them—in the traditional way, I fretted over word choices, went back and changed sentences, and accidentally left in a variety of typos that editors thankfully fixed.

For the AI content, I rotated between ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, and got the LLMs to write 10 articles with the same headlines and the same approximate number of words, for a tech-savvy audience. I even asked the AI apps to vary their language use, so that the output would "read less like an LLM has written it.".

In a recent development, pangram's AI text detector lets you upload files, but to make the task a little harder, I copied and pasted all of the text into the online article, so it wouldn't be able to rely on any metadata included in the file. The scans got the correct result each and every time: Human-written text came back as 100% human, and AI-written text came back as 100% AI.

Recent findings suggest that what's more, Pangram was certain about its results. All of the human writing was marked as highly likely to be human, and the vast majority of the AI writing was marked as highly likely to have come from an LLM. There were only a handful of phrases or sentences across thousands of AI words that got a "medium" rather than a "high" ranking for AI.

Sources indicate that now, there have been some edge cases where Pangram has got it wrong—like a poem repeating the same six words thousands of times—but as far as this sample goes, it can't be faulted. Clearly, my writing is too idiosyncratic and too clunky to be confused for the smooth sheen of AI-produced prose.

In a recent development, to be fair, I do have another advantage over AI: I can actually test out devices and apps in a way that LLM bots can't. ChatGPT can't experiment with One UI 9 (at least not yet), though it can scrape the web for various experiments and tests that real people have done.

Industry observers note that however, I was able to fool Pangram to some extent by alternating AI paragraphs with human-written paragraphs. The text was flagged as AI, but the percentage estimate was typically lower (20-25%) than what it actually was (around 50%). If you're offloading some but not all of your writing to AI, some of it might slip though as real.

Image and video detection is the newly introduced string to Pangram's bow, so I sifted through my phone's photo and video library for some pieces of content to test the AI on. Again, I used copy and paste to get the files into Pangram rather than uploading them, to limit how much information the AI detector could get from metadata.

Recent findings suggest that again, all the human-made content was recognized as such, with a very high level of certainty—whether it was complicated crowd shots or simpler images of natural scenes. Presumably, there are even more signals to go off than there are with writing, including camera movements, colors, style, consistency, and composition.

In a recent development, next up, I generated a few images and videos in Google Gemini and ChatGPT, requesting results that would look as photorealistic and "non-AI" as possible—the resulting files covered people, animals, and buildings. As before, I used copy, paste, and a few screengrabs to try and limit the metadata Pangram had access to.

Recent findings suggest that here, too, the AI identification was spot on, with all of the artificial content recognized as such, to a high level of confidence. This is perhaps not surprising: I think AI images and especially AI video still have more "tells" than AI writing, especially if you've seen a lot of it, so I wasn't expecting Pangram to fail here.

According to recent reports, I did try experimenting with real photos that had a little bit of AI in them, what with tools like Gemini and ChatGPT now so good at image editing, as well as creating pictures from scratch. These were marked as "unsure" by Pangram, though to cut it some slack, only a small amount of the images were altered.

As with the text, the best way to beat Pangram's detection systems seems to be to include some AI embedded in human-made content. It will most likely still fail the "100% human" test, but the tests I ran showed that Pangram is less certain in these cases, or underestimates the amount of AI there actually is.

Sources indicate that increase the level of AI, and the detection gets more reliable—but if you're only using AI for a small part of whatever it is you're making, it's less worthwhile using AI tools anyway. As far as these tests go, Pangram's claims about accuracy check out, making it a useful tool if you need to ensure something is AI-free.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

Recent findings suggest that tens of millions of people are playing Grand Theft Auto 6 right now. What’s the best way to experience Rockstar’s latest open-world epic? According to one of the developers themselves, you should play it with as little anxiety around checklists and online noise as possible.

âThere is so much to do in Leonida, and so much to discover, that we hope players get to the point where they stop thinking in tasks, completion percentages, online guides and rather let the game unfold in front of them,” VP of design Stephen Donkin said in a packet of studio development notes shared with press. “When you play the game and take your time with it, playing at the pace it asks you to, it can really unfold in front of you in a way that can feel almost infinite at a macro level, but each individual encounter still feels hand-crafted and with a human behind it.

Recent findings suggest that donkin’s first Rockstar credit was as a QA tester on GTA 5, and his advice for GTA 6 players echoed the feelings of some of the studio’s other developers when it comes to taking in the immersive beauty and emergent nuance of the new entry’s complex world. âThere are clearly tons of high-stakes, high-energy, fast-paced moments and thrills and laughs along the way, but there are also quiet, meditative experiences and adventures to be had that offer a fully different feeling,” said senior design director Ghyan Koehne. “If I had to be held to a single feeling, Iâd say âwonder.â We want players to be constantly presented with a feeling of wonderâwe hope everyone feels a mixture of emotions.â.

It’s a stark contrast to how GTA lives in the popular imagination of most people, which is as a chaos sim full of drugs, sex, and violent crime. GTA 6 has those things, but they are far less domineering parts of the experience this time around. It’s also completely divorced from how some people often experience modern video games, which is heavily augmented by a second-screen experience full of achievement guides, TikTok memes, and social media rage-bait.

According to recent reports, people should play GTA 6 however they want, but I’d encourage them to take at least a few hours to experience the game in the dark with headphones on and as little knowledge as possible of what awaits them and how the whole thing works, their phones and laptops safely tucked away in a different room. Former Kotaku editor Kirk Hamilton was famous for telling people to turn off parts of the onscreen UI to make the experience more immersive and make it feel less like a chore list. Every substantial newly introduced open-world game that came out there would be a post about turning off the minimap.

Sources indicate that I’ve never been able to play games that way. I’m too fidgety and squirrely for that kind of thing. But I always try to spend at least a couple hours in that headspace, treating what’s in front of me more as something worth experiencing for its own sake than just as a maze to speedrun through as efficiently as possible in exchange for in-game rewards, entertaining setpieces, and satisfying emotional climaxes. That’s an increasingly alien way of approaching anything in our algorithmically optimized world, but GTA 6 offers as good a reason as any to try it.

“If players can let go and submit to becoming immersed in the world of Leonida, and just follow their nose as they play, they will feel the Leonida I have felt,” Donkin said, “And thatâs all we could ask for.â.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L’Oréal Paris welcomed its latest Women of Worth honorees with an intimate, elegant gala in Los Angeles on Wednesday night. For the annual celebration, which honors unsung nonprofit leaders, guests gathered at The Ebell of Los Angeles, a venue with a rich history of its own.

The evening began with an outdoor cocktail hour, where guests enjoyed passed apps and specialty drinks like the “Parisian Refresher” and “Worth It Spritz” under sparkling bistro lights. As honorees and attendees mixed and mingled, they also had the opportunity to pose for a photographer and peruse a beauty bar stocked with L’Oréal Paris-brand lipsticks, lip oils, and glosses, which were available for guests to take home in a plush velvet bag with “I’m Worth It” embroidered on it.

As the gala officially began inside The Ebell’s picturesque ballroom, longtime brand ambassador Eva Longoria gave the introductory remarks, noting that “this night always gives me goosebumps. I’m always crying.” She saluted her 20-plus-year partnership with the brand and joked that it made her “112 years old,” though she doesn’t look like it, the actor-director noted, “because I use Revitalift.” She gave a shout-out to the many beauty influencers in attendance, including Laura Lee and Desi Perkins. “You guys really changed the game of beauty, and I just applaud you,” she said. “Put me in your TikToks.”.

Recent findings suggest that L’Oréal Paris USA president Laura Branik followed Longoria, emphasizing the brand’s commitment to and pride in its Women of Worth program, which continues to celebrate “the power of women who know their worth and use it,” she remarked. She then welcomed the tech giant’s newest global ambassador, Kristen Bell, to the stage. Bell, who was attending her “first Women of Worth ever,” said she was “very happy to be here” and introduced moving presentations for the first two honorees: Vy Le of WhereWear, which transforms clothing donations into targeted support for women’s and housing-insecure shelters and the people they serve, and Amanda Rice of The Chick Mission, a nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that every young woman newly diagnosed with cancer has the option to preserve her fertility.

According to recent reports, actor and brand ambassador Aja Naomi King was up next, taking note of the room full of glamorous gowns and festive energy. “Everyone showed up and showed out,” she said, “and we appreciate that because these women deserve to be celebrated properly. I had the immense honor of helping select this year’s Women of Worth, and I keep thinking about how much it matters when someone believes in your potential.” King introduced two honorees: Maya Bird-Murphy of Mobile Makers, an award-winning nonprofit that expands access to design education through workshops, community engagement, public installations, and pop-ups, and Christy Vogel of Sounding Joy, a nonprofit dedicated to providing hearing aids to children whose families cannot afford them.

Longoria then returned to present another pair of honorees: Marisa Hamamoto of Infinite Flow Dance, an award-winning disability-led nonprofit and professional dance manufacturer with a mission to reimagine possibilities, one dance at a time, and Chanel Power of Mentor Me Collective, a technical institute transforming how emerging technologists are identified, developed, and positioned to lead.

In a recent development, during a break in the program, guests enjoyed dinner from a menu that included roast chicken, citrus-soy-and-apple-cider-braised short ribs, and vegan pan-seared “scallops.” Another highlight? The venue’s bathrooms were stocked with more coveted L’Oréal Paris goods like lip oil, mascara, setting spray, and velour puff makeup applicators.

Following the break, ambassador, actor, and model Cara Delevingne led the room in a cheerful group proclamation of “We’re worth it!” before introducing her honorees: Emily Cho of Juvie for STEM (JSTEM), an international nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to high-quality STEM education for justice-involved youth, and Arielle Galinsky of The Legacy Project, Inc. (TLP), a national nonprofit connecting younger and older adults for multigenerational friendship and storytelling.

Legacy L’Oréal Paris ambassador Andie MacDowell had the pleasure of introducing the event’s final honorees. “For 40 years I have been a part of the L’Oréal Paris family,” she stated, with the milestone receiving enthusiastic applause from the audience. “After all these years, the thing that stays with me [about the Women of Worth honorees] is the determination to make life better for someone else. That kind of care is powerful.” MacDowell introduced Jordan Pine of Greenlight Operation, a Pennsylvania nonprofit that strives to strategically combat human trafficking and serve sex trafficked women through a continuum of restorative care, and Dr. Christie Brungardt, cofounder of Jana’s Campaign, a Kansas-based nonprofit dedicated to preventing gender and relationship violence through education.

Proud “newbie” Bell returned to the stage to offer closing remarks and thank all the honorees for their tireless efforts to make life better for others. “I will be thinking of all 10 of these stories and the women we met tonight for quite some time,” she remarked. “Even though their stories couldn’t be more different, they seem to have one thing in common: that they all saw what needed to change and they did it. They didn’t wait for someone else to do something; they stepped forward and they did it themselves. And honestly, I think that’s gonna be my biggest takeaway from my first Women of Worth celebration ever: Never underestimate what one woman can set in motion.”.

Each of the 10 Women of Worth 2026 honorees received a $25,000 grant, mentorship, and national visibility. As the program concluded, honorees, their proud guests, and other attendees continued to soak up the special evening and shared in a few more hugs and photo ops. Before departing for the evening, guests were invited to enjoy a final “sweet moment” in a separate room where a colorful candy bar and glasses of Champagne awaited.

It has been revealed that the Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this week's offering is another nice find at a price that can't be beat. Every Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free games is create a free Epic account and enable two-factor authentication. You have a week to add the freebies to your library before the latest one(s) take their place. At this point, Epic has given away hundreds of free games, and there's no sign that the program will stop any time soon. The company has also extended its freebies to Android devices, and you can claim a free game every week here as well. We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free games and next week's offerings. If you're looking for more freebies, you can check out our list of the 25 best free PC games to play right now, or for more options, the 25 best free games to play on multiple platforms. Current free game at Epic This week's free game is Mark of the Deep, a 2025 pirate-themed adventure with a mix of Metroidvania and soulslike gameplay. Next free games at Epic Next week, you can get a welcome gift pack for Firestone: Idle Clicker Online RPG, and you can help a pair of penguins out in the co-op platformer Bread & Fred. See all free games at Epic Epic Games Store free games list We're keeping a running list of every free game that Epic users have been able to claim in the past. From AAA hits to indie darlings, Epic has really made its mark with free games. You can even snag these games if you don't have a powerful PC so you can play them if you ever get one. Look at the list below to see the frankly ridiculous list of free games that have been available. Industry News: GTA 6's massive casino and sick go-kart track are at the moment closed, but I'm hoping we can trust those 'coming soon' signs 🙏

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I'd just stolen my very first airplane in GTA 6 and was happily cruising over the city when I looked out my window and saw an enormous purple building.
  • According to recent reports, oh, hell yes.
  • Trust me, I tried every door, and the only one that opened was a utility closet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I'd just stolen my very first airplane in GTA 6 and was happily cruising over the city when I looked out my window and saw an enormous purple building. I banked, slowed down, and flew a bit closer to read the huge sign on the roof.

According to recent reports, oh, hell yes. I was so excited to throw my carefully accumulated three hundred dollars away on poker and slots that I immediately attempted my very first landing. After the explosion and my miraculous resurrection, I rushed back to the casino and crashed again, this time with my body into the locked front doors.

The casino in GTA 6 is closed. Trust me, I tried every door, and the only one that opened was a utility closet.

I was early into my playthrough, still in Chapter 1 of the GTA 6 story missions, so I thought maybe there'll be some mission that unlocks the casino so I can play some poker, try my luck at the slots, and maybe bet on the also-closed dog track—I assume it's a dog track because I've seen dogs in GTA 6, but no horses—that's right next door to the casino.

Industry observers note that nope! I'm now 100% done with the main story and that casino is still closed. And that's not the only business in GTA 6 that isn't open for business. Not even a half-mile away from the casino there's a go-cart track called Hot Skidz sporting a huge "Coming Soon" sign. I saw that early in my game as well, and checked back later. Still closed. I also found a second, smaller casino. Also closed.

What a letdown. I managed to get my motorcycle onto the go-cart track, and as I drove glumly around it, alone, having no fun, I perked up a bit. Maybe this just gives me something to look forward to. A hint of more singleplayer content that'll be coming to GTA 6 next year. Hopefully next year.

There's already a lot of seemingly unfinished stuff in GTA 6, partial systems that could be added to and completed, like:.

I felt better after that, but as I went back to stare at that huge, closed casino—which is all lit up at night like it's actually open, even though it is not open, and I know this because I rechecked all the doors—I remembered how the casino in GTA 5 worked. It came to the game post launch, but only as part of GTA Online. It never opened in singleplayer.

But surely, why include the building at all in GTA 6 singleplayer if it wasn't also going to be in singleplayer? They wouldn't do that to us, would they? They wouldn't open it in GTA 6 Online and not open it in GTA 6 singleplayer.

Recent findings suggest that that would be like putting dozens of dogs in a game and not letting us have our own dog. Madness.

Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1387 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change.
  • Industry observers note that download your playlist as a .txt file.
  • Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change. The main reason is AI-made music: Tidal has stricter AI filtering than any other major streamer. The second reason is audio quality. While all major music streaming services do basically the same thing, Tidal's focus has always been on streaming music at the highest possible quality. While other streaming services have more or less "caught up" in terms of pure sonic fidelity, Tidal still is better at getting that quality to your speakers, if you know a few tricks.

Industry observers note that download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

Install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Sources indicate that download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

Run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Recent findings suggest that sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Sources indicate that have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

According to recent reports, like most streaming services, Tidal has a "heart" button called "add to my collection." You can click on any track, album, or playlist to "like" and saved it. But Tidal also has a separate, somewhat mysterious "Save for Later" option that puts songs, albums, and playlists into a separate collection. There are a couple reasons for this. First, it keeps a running list of upcoming-to-you music waiting for you on a rainy day, and secondly, it (presumably) affects your recommendation algorithm differently. While Tidal isn't open about every detail of its recommendation algorithm, I assume "save for later" has less weight (if any) on your future recommendations than "add to my collection.".

On Tidal, tracks that are 100% AI-generated get an "AI" badge, earn no royalties, and are never placed on a Tidal-curated playlist. Customers can flip a switch in Settings to either allow or disallow AI content, too. Simple, but there's a bit of nuance that goes beyond the on/off switch. You have to set the AI-toggle separately on each device you use Tidal on, even if it's the same account. I guess this is so I can listen to AI music in my car but not at my desk? Sadly, AI detection is not a science, so some AI-made, and partly AI-made, tracks may still get through.

In a recent development, if you're streaming music from a music app through Bluetooth, the output is automatically compressed to a lower quality, and your phone stays in charge, so a phone call or a notification can interrupt your music. But Tidal's Tidal Connect feature skips the middleman. Music streams directly from your wifi to your speaker and your phone becomes a remote control, so you can take a call, go for a walk, and even run out of phone battery and the music will keep playing.

Have an external device with Tidal Connect compatibility.

Make sure your speaker or other output device and phone or computer are on the same wifi network.

Pick your speaker on your wifi network.

Click the icon again to switch back to your phone.

It has been revealed that plenty of wifi speakers don’t support Tidal Connect, so check before you buy. Tidal keeps the full list of supported devices on its site. There's everything there from WiiM Mini—a $99 small box that adds Tidal Connect to speakers you already own—to dCS components that cost more than a car.

Industry observers note that tidal Connect isn't the only way to get the highest quality audio from Tidal. You can go for an old school, wired path like I have. I play audio from my desktop and route it directly to a mixer via USB. Here's the set-up:.

Settings > Streaming > Audio Quality: Max.

Sound Output: choose your mixer as the output device instead of your computer’s speakers.

It has been revealed that exclusive Mode: On. It’s under Sound Output > More Settings. Tidal sends audio straight to the mixer at each track’s native sample rate, without your computer resampling it or mixing in system sounds.

Recent findings suggest that force Volume. It's in the desktop app next to Exclusive Mode, under Settings > Streaming > Sound Output > More Settings. Force Volume means Tidal will always output at the highest volume. You'll be controlling the actual volume from your mixer.

Set your levels with the mixer’s faders.

To check what your mixer can handle, look at its maximum sample rate:.

In a recent development, mac: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications > Utilities), click your mixer, and open the Format menu. The highest number listed is your ceiling.

Windows: Go to Settings > System > Sound, click your mixer, and look under Output settings > Format.

My cheap-ass mixer tops out a 16-bit/48kHz which is CD quality, but not Tidal's top of 24-bit/192kHz, but at least I can control the EQ. Speaking of...

It has been revealed that it's much cooler to turn dials than mess with computer settings. Tidal doesn’t have an equalizer, so if you’re using Tidal Connect or a wired connection, you'll need something to shape the sound. Here are some options:.

Recent findings suggest that your computer: System-wide EQ apps, like Equalizer APO on Windows or SoundSource on Mac, can adjust Tidal’s output. They don’t work with Tidal Connect though, which bypasses your computer’s audio processing.

Your speaker’s app: If you use a Tidal Connect speaker or streamer, it probably has a companion app for EQ.

A mixer or audio interface: Channel EQ knobs let you adjust bass, mids, and treble by hand, in real time.

Your speakers: Many powered speakers and studio monitors have low and high controls on the back.

A stereo receiver or amp: Old-school bass and treble knobs still work in 2026.

Most of Tidal's catalog streams as "better-than-CD quality" FLAC files at every subscription tier, so you might be inclined to click "play music at highest quality on everything." but settings are only as good as the gear you're using, and there are times when lower quality is the right choice. Here's when to turn down the settings:.

When you're in your car: CarPlay and Bluetooth cut audio down to CD quality or less before it reaches your speaker, and with road noises, it usually doesn't matter anyway, so turn the streaming down to "High" instead of "Max." Or download your playlist before you leave, if you must have "as good as possible" audio.

You have a data cap and are off wifi. Top quality audio requires huge file transfer, so set your mobile data to High or Low and save Max for wifi.

Your connection is spotty: To avoid buffering, a lower setting keeps the music playing.

Recent findings suggest that this isn't a universal hack, but some Android phones have microSD card slots, which can save you a lot of hassle if you're downloading a lot of audio files—an album at high quality might top 1GB, so having an external source will save you a ton of hassle. If your phone has a microSD card slot, go to Tidal's settings, find "download destination" and choose the memory card.
