One of the most prominent figures of the so-called Bluenami was not a candidate on the ballot, but rather a Twitch streamer and political commentator: Hasan Piker.

This year Hasan was involved in dozens of races across the country, campaigning for progressive candidates like Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed. But you’re probably more likely to associate Hasan’s name with what other people have had to say about him—from Fox News commentators to more established members of the Democratic Party.

Sources indicate that hasan regularly courts controversy on both his hours-long Twitch streams, where he’s mentioned things like “America deserved 9/11,” and social media, where he’s written that Hamas “is a thousand times better than” Israel. He claims he’s often taken out of context, and that his audience knows what he really means—and where he stands. In his mind, he’s a leftist provocateur, maybe, but one who understands the importance of working-class values and electoral strategy.

While Hasan has walked back some of his more inflammatory language, his rhetoric raises the question: Is he a liability to the cause he champions? Or is he successfully reaching the critical audience—namely, young men—that helped elect the wave of progressives poised to take office in January?

According to recent reports, with 2028 on the horizon, I wanted to know how Hasan thinks about his growing platform, and if he sees his role shifting in the media landscape. What responsibility does he have to his viewers and to the candidates he supports? And does he regret any of those past statements?

We also got into the DSA’s more extreme positions and how to make sense of them; why he thinks the Republicans put his thirst trap on the jumbotron at their convention; and how he, a self-proclaimed socialist, thinks about his own money.

Mark Guiducci: Hasan Piker, welcome to Fair Game.

Hasan Piker: Very excited to be here.

Industry observers note that thanks for coming. Hasan, you are more online than just about anyone. You spend at least seven hours a day streaming. You reach tens of thousands of people at a time on average, and it’s all in the channel that you control. I’m curious, what are you doing here with me today? Why are you showing up for a show with a legacy media publication? What’s in it for you?

Well, I saw the clips and everybody looked really good. The lighting was perfect. I saw the Dari[aliza Avila Chevalier] clips, I saw Ta-Nehisi [Coates], and I was like, I got to get in on that.

Yeah. So shouts out to the team. You guys did a phenomenal job lighting this up. It looks very cool too.

It has been revealed that okay. We’ll take the compliment.

In a recent development, but the serious answer is, I mean, I reach an audience that obviously does not watch television, does not read legacy publications at all. And I want to show people that read Vanity Fair that I am not a terrorist.

It has been revealed that right. Which brings me to my next question because—.

Yeah, exactly. That would be the name of the episode. You’ve been everywhere this year, and you became this kind of bogeyman for the right, who probably have never heard you, watched your stream, or heard anything you’ve said out of your mouth. They’ve just heard quotes repeated by news anchors. And not even just for the right, even for some on the left. And you played this interesting role because you were a surrogate and a media figure and then a media figure covering the media as well. I want to spend a little bit of time talking about how you see your role. And to start, do you consider yourself a journalist?

Okay. Because it’s like you present this interesting new type of figure. I was thinking about how you’ve done an interview with CNN, you’ve done interviews with MS NOW, but they don’t have you on as much as I would expect them to.

I have some thoughts, but I wonder why you think that is.

I think I’ve pissed off a bunch of executives over there, because, in my experience, there are plenty of amazing reporters and journalists and producers that I know that work at all of these newsrooms, right? But from what I have seen, the masthead has a very different editorial slant than sometimes what the reporters want to cover.

Because they talk about you a lot.

Industry observers note that they talk about me a lot. And also I’ve never been invited on any of these outlets as a pundit either, which is also strange because, as you also pointed to, I don’t just operate as a campaignster. As a matter of fact, that’s something I did very briefly and I did not like it at all. I’m first and foremost a commentator…. I do have the capacity to do journalism at times. I’ll do interviews with candidates. I’ll go out and—.

Recent findings suggest that well, candidates I like. Sometimes I do interviews with candidates I don’t like or I’m unsure about as well. The problem is most of the candidates don’t want to come on if they know I’m gonna cook ’em. Like Gavin Newsom, I have had feelers out to get him on the broadcast.

I have. Gavin, Gavin, come on the show. I am a taxpaying California resident. I’m one of your constituents. You want to be president in 2028, you’re gonna have to be able to talk to people like myself.

All right. So, Hasan, this cycle you were involved in some way in, by one count, 48 different candidates’ races, and AIPAC and pro-Israel groups spent about $101 million in those races. And on Election Day, your stream was the second most watched in the country after NBC News’s “Kornacki Cam.” With a little bit of distance, how are you thinking about what happened a couple of weeks ago, both for yourself and for the country?

I feel a lot of hope. Hopefully it’s not going to be short-lived. But I feel very excited for the first time in a very long time, after 10 years of some of the most odious politics that we’ve seen from Trumpism, from MAGA. We finally saw a real sea change through electoralism. People truly have had enough with Trumpism.

I wouldn’t be so certain because I feel like if there’s one controlled opposition party that is capable of breathing life back into MAGA, it would be the establishment Democrats. So I’m a little bit worried, but it’s very clear that people are truly fed up.

All right. So there are a couple of different narratives that are coming out of the midterms right now. Rahm Emanuel, for instance, is touting this as a victory for moderate Democrats, saying that they ran 21 points above Kamala Harris. The DSA, meanwhile, is claiming that American voters have “emphatically endorsed socialism.” Other pundits are saying that these significant gains have nothing to do with the Democrats and are actually about the war in Iran and high gas prices. So does this debate between moderates and progressives feel like a healthy back-and-forth to you, or does this feel like the upcoming aisle that has to be straddled?

Industry observers note that I mean, I think this is not even a latest debate. This factional battle has existed within the Democratic Party and perhaps—.

Yeah, but the progressive wing was always really fringe.

It has been revealed that and now we’re talking about—I don’t know if 50/50 is right. I don’t want to use numbers, but—.

According to recent reports, I think it’s a testament to our success, especially in the midterms, that there are a lot of people who are trying to protect their comfortable sinecures and are outright panicking. And all of that completely sidesteps the reality that the vulgar Bernie-ism of 2016 was echoed through every single candidacy, every single campaign all across the country, from the obvious Berniecrats like Abdul El-Sayed to even people like Roy Cooper, who in the past were very moderate, very centrist. And he still is a center-right figure, which clearly works in North Carolina. But even he was railing against data centers, billionaires, the uncertainty surrounding AI. I mean, this is left populism. And that rhetoric, one could say, was deployed in the past by even the likes of Bill Clinton and Al Gore.

It has been revealed that but for some strange reason, there was a turning point in 2016 where the Democratic Party adopted this strange role of defending the corporate class and defending the elites and took ownership over, I guess, defending these institutions overall. And these institutions are worthy of defending, for the record. However, from the perspective of the masses, if the government is failing them, if these institutions are failing them, then they wanted someone to break it. And that was obviously the right populism of Donald Trump. And break those institutions, he surely did. And we’ve seen the devastating results of that.

So you credit the progressivism with what happened on election night?

Absolutely. I mean, there’s certainly local moderation on issues, right? Because James Talarico went from saying “God is nonbinary” to “we need to defend our transgender brothers and sisters, our neighbors,” which is, again, insanely woke for Texas, or just in general, right? There are far more conservative figures in the party than James Talarico’s current position on the trans problem.

According to recent reports, okay. But sometimes the way that you run—oftentimes the way that you run needs to be different than the way that you govern or lead once you’re there. Do you think it is productive to continue pushing some of the farther-left ideas once they get to Congress? Or is pragmatism and getting things done, you know, defining things that are really achievable and sticking to them as a bloc, as a group, and pushing them over the line— when you’re talking to some of these winners, are you talking about [that]?

I think if I could speak to the entire incoming freshman class or the entire caucus—.

I would say, be bold, be brave, and obviously immediately implement accountability. Investigations are an absolute must. This is what people are demanding. After the economy, the second concern, the biggest concern, is corruption. The second term with Trump has been unbelievable. I mean, look, I’m Turkish. I’ve seen corruption in the Turkish government. I’ve seen corruption and tracked it and talked about it all around the world with different governments. I’ve never seen anything like what the Trump administration has done because of how flagrant and in your face it was. And I think people responded to that, finally, in the appropriate way they should, with anger.

So you’re calling for subpoenas and investigations.

It has been revealed that I think impeachment, especially for Trump, is probably the last thing that I care about. I mean, I want these guys to go to jail. Let’s be clear. If they’ve done the crime, they need to do the time. I don’t think anyone is above the law. We have to restore law and order. So I’m a law-and-order Democrat. And I know that sounds something very different in Washington, DC, or in general. I think when politicians say that, they mean, like, punish the poor for minor crimes. I’m talking about punishing the wealthy for their corruption, for their major crimes, because they’re the ones who are robbing people blind.

But, you know, a lot of people would say that impeachment would be a distraction. So I guess what I’m saying is, if you had to choose three agenda items that the Democrats are agreeing on and they’re going forward with—you already noted subpoenas and investigations.

What else? What are the other two that in the first year you really want to see happen?

Recent findings suggest that I think it’s virtually impossible [with] the current DOJ to—they’re not impartial, right? I don’t think that we are going to move the needle on actual criminal investigations before the Democrats win the White House in 2028. But all of this is building up for that moment. And for that reason, I think we need to talk about affordability—and not just simply talk about affordability, but also explain how we’re going to solve the affordability crisis through a comprehensive legislative agenda. And one of the major concerns around affordability that is oftentimes discussed as a separate thing, but it’s not, is health care. And the Democratic Party’s approach to health care has been lackluster. Even though Americans obviously overwhelmingly trust the Democrats with fixing health care or solving the problem with health care, the reality of the matter is, while the ACA was a fantastic improvement to what existed previously, it’s not enough, and we have to move the needle in a healthier direction. We have to push for a single-payer health care solution.

Industry observers note that I’m perfectly fine with that. I’ve joked about that for years ’cause he’s so invested. He’s such a petty despot and so narcissistic that—.

Yes. I have pitched this over and over again on my show. Look, you win so massive with Donald Trump if you go to Donald Trump and you say, “Look, Obamacare, not the best, right? Now you get to destroy Obamacare and you get to build something else in your name. We call it Trumpcare. It’s single-payer. It’s Medicare for All.” I think he would do it.

In a recent development, look at this. Bipartisan collaboration.

Yes, I’m pragmatic. I’m bipartisan.

All right, so let’s take a step back. You were talking a second ago about how Talarico was woke. And on November 4, Twitter, formerly known as X, was amazing. Memes, jokes, you know.

In a recent development, I see what you did there. Yeah. We flipped it back.

It has been revealed that yeah, we flipped it back. With the Democrats’ victory, the idea that woke was back, do you think that’s true? Do you think that we’re going to see, culturally, the return of this idea of woke? And do you think that’s a good thing for the Democrats?

Yes. I do think that the pendulum swing was an inevitability. I talked about this quite a bit. I saw the early warning signs when [Joe] Biden won. That was one of my major warnings that young men were going to go back to the Gamergate era of very far-right politics because the Biden administration was not delivering. And what ended up happening with this anti-woke narrative, this culture war that the Republicans had seemingly won, that they presented as a mandate, right, was some of the most odious commentary, some of the most vile rhetoric that anyone had ever seen.

Industry observers note that definitely. The idea of woke now, though, I'm just curious—being politically correct or precise in one’s language was, for a time, an outward indication of being a progressive or maybe even being a good person in culture. Do you think that’s still the case?

In a recent development, I mean, I’m progressive, so I think so, but I’m a little biased. But I will say this: I think that there were certainly social excesses, which is ironic because this whole Woke 1.0, 2.0 distinction, I feel a little responsible for in the discourse because I jokingly used to say—.

Yeah, now I’ve joked about that too, and now journalists are reaching out to me being like, “Do you think Woke 3.0 is real?” I’m like, “I’m joking, guys. It’s not serious.” But here’s the thing, there is a little bit of sincerity there. I think one of the things that I routinely criticized during that 2016-to-2022, 2023, era of, I guess, Woke 1.0 was the social excesses, the maximalist demands, the inability to understand that people are complex and don’t have the same lived experience that everybody else has. I always would get so frustrated because we on the left say America’s a white supremacist country, and yet we don’t ever reflect on what kind of social conditioning comes along with that. So that if you do actually hear someone engage in a microaggression, for example, that we have to be a little bit more understanding and try to ease them into the conversation.

Industry observers note that and on the other side, people will say, “Oh, that’s normalizing this kind of behavior. It’s unacceptable.” And I totally see the other side of that argument as well, but I think, especially if you’re campaigning or especially if you’re building a movement, you do have to be a little bit more understanding and not be so hardheaded and assume that everyone has to agree with you from the jump without you making a convincing case as to why you might be correct.

According to recent reports, okay. All right. So we’ve talked a lot about what you think about the political landscape, but I want to talk also about your role in it right now and going forward. So initially, you were called the Joe Rogan of the left. Recently, you’ve said you operate more like a Charlie Kirk. Is that the right analog for the kind of influence you want to have? And if not, is there another?

It has been revealed that I don’t think there is an appropriate analog because I’m everything all at once at the same time, because I work out and I do collaborations with people who are not expressly political, so that’s kind of like Joe Rogan. I go out and operate sometimes as a campaign surrogate, and I do rallies at college campuses and I deliver speeches, so that’s kind of like Charlie Kirk. But then usually my day-to-day commentary is what I like to jokingly refer to as a Rush Limbaugh for Zoomers. So I do all of those things at the same time, and that’s, I think, part of the reason why it’s so hard to make sense of what I do from the perspective of someone who just doesn’t understand Twitch or doesn’t understand exactly what I’m doing and has only seen negatively framed clips or clips out of context, that kind of thing. Having noted that, on the political-ideological side of things, of course I am the furthest from all of those figures. I’m just talking about the form and function of it all.

In a recent development, okay. So it seems like you’ve been recently the guy that progressives come to when they’re trying to run a primary from the left, but then when they get to the general or to office, maybe they don’t need you as much, or they have left you behind, or they distanced themselves from you. And I think about [Zohran] Mamdani in this case. I just—.

According to recent reports, maybe because of that Rush Limbaugh–esque heightened rhetoric; do you agree with that characterization? And how does that make you feel?

Well, my feelings are immaterial in this. As long as they’re delivering, I think that’s what matters. I’ve said this before: I love Zohran and, off the rip, my attitude on this was always just put the policies in the bag. If you’re delivering for the people of Newly introduced York, and if you’re delivering successfully and every success that you have as a democratic socialist mayor of New York bodes well for the rest of this movement, then I’m happy.

Yeah, but are you talking to him behind the scenes? There’s still a relationship there? Because honestly—.

Recent findings suggest that yes. But the thing is, what I’m doing is too fresh for people to fully realize, to fully comprehend. So of course there’s going to be some growing pains as far as how to navigate through an unbelievably contentious media environment, especially if the candidate[s] themselves are Muslim. And, you know, I think that is the reason why—the two major figures that I can point to that have done a little bit of distancing, at least in rhetoric, even though they never disavow the platform, disavow the person, they just say, “Oh, I don’t agree with that statement”—those two figures are Abdul El-Sayed and Zohran Mamdani. They’re both very progressive. One’s a democratic socialist, the other one’s not, but they’re still very progressive for American politics, and they’re Muslim. I think that is a substantial part of the reason why I’ve given them a lot more bandwidth to operate in this space in whichever way they want to, because the expectation or the fears that they have are very real. As someone who has been at the center of a lot of this manufactured outrage, a lot of this controversy, being presented as an Islamist, jihadist at times, a terrorist, I know the role that the first Muslim senator has to play on the campaign trail. So on that front, of course they got to do what they got to do.

So you intellectually understand it, but do you feel used?

I would only feel that way if they did not follow through on their promises that they made on the campaign trail. If Abdul came out tomorrow and was like, “Money out of politics? Maybe money in politics. Money in your pocket? Maybe you don’t get money in your pocket. Medicare for All? Medicare for some”—if he were to just flip the script on not just me, but Michiganders and America as a whole, then I would feel very betrayed.

According to recent reports, so we talked a little bit earlier about your audience at the very beginning. You know, you’re an interesting figure for them. There are a significant number of them that are with you for hours on end a day, and I think they probably look up to you. What responsibility do you feel to the people who watch your streams?

As far as the responsibilities that I have, I am very aware of them. I see myself as, in some respects, NPR for Zoomers. For many people, and now even an older audience as well, I am their primary news outlet. They have me on in the background, and I’m offering news and commentary throughout the day while they’re going through and doing their chores or at work with me blasting in one ear. So I know that if I were to stop randomly, people would feel it, because I see it as—I listen to The Daily; I listen to NPR every morning. If somehow I wake up one morning and NPR is no longer on, I’d be like, What happened? How am I gonna figure out what’s going on in the world?

Yeah, that’s just a lot of pressure, though, because NPR has a whole staff of people that, [if] someone’s sick, someone can pinch-hit.

I mean, I’m fine living in that environment. I’m happy to do it. I’m happy to take on that responsibility.

Can I ask, what’s your personal life like right now? I mean, that is a lot of time on the air, and probably you have to read the news yourself too. So are you seeing friends a lot? Do you see your family a lot?

I keep my private life private for obvious reasons ’cause there are a lot of insane people out there. But yes, I do spend a good deal of time with friends and family. I have normie friends as well that are just completely removed from the world of politics and from the world of Hollywood, influencers, that kind of thing.

According to recent reports, yeah, no, they keep me grounded, for sure, and my family certainly does as well. I spend every waking moment that I’m not on camera doing things like that, you know, enjoying the finer things in life.

Do you think of yourself as a role model?

In some respects, yes. I don’t think people should follow everything that I do to a T, but I definitely do see that. I recognize the responsibility that influencers have over so many people, and I try to put my best foot forward in an effort to cultivate a nicer space on the internet, one that is more productive for people. I try to urge people to go out and unionize in their workplaces, join the Democratic Socialists of America, but then also at the same time, I try to get them to go out and work out. I’m very open about my fitness journey, my health journey. And the same even goes for my presentation. I’ve gone through these different eras now on my broadcast. Right now we’re in the suit arc. And then I sometimes see that reflected in the crowd as well when I go out to these rallies. I start seeing people also wearing suits, which is a little strange to experience, but it’s not the worst thing, right?

I think that’s a good influence.

Recent findings suggest that yeah, I think that is a good influence. You’re rocking a nice suit yourself.

According to recent reports, I bought this at a photo shoot for Days magazine. This stylist had pulled this and I loved it.

I literally was like, “I’m buying this from you.” And then since then, she’s been pulling stuff for me.

In a recent development, can I ask, are you having fun? Because it seems like you are, but then what we were talking about before, with the way that you might feel abandoned—and especially the past few months, this cycle, has it been fun?

In a recent development, no, it has not been fun. I don’t think it’s great to be called a terrorist and lied about and slandered endlessly with the hopes that this could potentially tank the Democratic Party’s chances of bringing about accountability to this fascist administration. I did not enjoy that.

Industry observers note that and I certainly also did not enjoy the fact that I was kind of left out on my own a little bit, where—of course I got a lot of support from the movement, DSA, and the wonderful slate of candidates that we worked with, but I’ve never had institutional backing. And as a matter of fact, there was a lot of anxiety from the institution that is the Democratic Party. So all of its loyal servants were going on TV and being like, “He’s a horrible person who needs to go away,” over and over again. So that didn’t feel great. ’Cause there’s always negative polarization when Trump attacks someone and the Republicans attack someone, but if there isn’t any backing from the liberal side, even from a partisan perspective, then that complicates things. All of a sudden you’re like, Okay, well, who’s on my side now? I have nobody to push back.

You’re playing this game where you try to find the worst quotes that you can and frame them as negatively as you can, and then attack candidates that might not even know the context behind some of these words. Bernie was, I think, the best, ironically enough, at dealing with it when he was asked by Abby Phillip. He called me a radio man, which is funny. He’s been on the show, still doesn’t know what I do, which is fine. That’s unc, that’s grand-unc. But he basically said, “Look, everybody indicates silly things. I mean, he talks for thousands of hours. He’s a radio man. And not only does everybody say silly things, but ultimately there’s a reason why he has such a passionate fan base, because we agree on the broad spectrum of issues that he advocates for, and so do all of his fans. So to reduce someone to a couple of choice clips is obviously going to never give you the full picture.” I mean, he didn’t use all those words.

It’s not about being a person; it’s about being a cudgel, just something that you can use as a counterbalance.

It has been revealed that I don’t think liberals, and even the left broadly, [are] ready for how to deal with that because we’ve never really had a person like me in the past. I mean, the Republicans obviously have three to four decades of this, coming from William F. Buckley all the way to Rush Limbaugh and Charlie Kirk and numerous other far-right figures, that they know how to brush this aside. I mean, JD Vance, when asked about his affiliation with Tucker Carlson, will be like, “He’s my friend.” And that’s it. That’s that.

Industry observers note that okay. So you’re streaming most of the day, you’re reacting to news in real time, and just even by your own admission, you’ve said some—I think you said “silly things.” I would say some pretty extreme things along the way.

It has been revealed that and I know you’ve walked back past statements. “America deserved 9/11”—how many times have you heard that this season? Quote: “If you cared about Medicare fraud, you’d kill Rick Scott.” You’ve said things that you wish you had said differently. Do you regret anything that you’ve said? Because I think regret is different than “wish I said differently.”.

It’s a tough one. I mean, look, I probably will regret things that I will say in the future as well. It’s virtually impossible for me not to say things—.

Industry observers note that yeah, it is, but it also isn’t because I have apologized and taken back some of the things that I’ve said and apologized for how I worded or framed things. But do I regret it? I mean, I feel like I’m stronger as a consequence of all of those experiences at the same time, so I don’t know.

Do you feel like someone in your role has a different responsibility with their words or their public platform than an elected official or even a journalist?

It has been revealed that okay. But you also said that you are a role model.

Can you parse that a little bit?

In a recent development, yeah, absolutely. It goes back to the space that I occupy and what I try to do with it. Right? I don’t think that I am, at least to my audience or anyone else that’s paying attention, doing anything that’s remotely politically as toxic as the way that the current systems operate. The rude behavior that I demonstrate is what people get frustrated by or what they attack, but—.

Yeah, I am vulgar, for sure. But I think the systems of violence and oppression that people are subjected to [are] far worse than any vulgar thing I could have ever noted. And we kind of saw this dynamic play itself out on the campaign trail as well. And I think the finality of it all came with Haley Stevens, when she decided to lean into the “Hasan Piker is such a problem that I'm leaving the Democratic Party and endorsing the Republican platform.” [That] was, I think in some respects, a wake-up call because it forced everyone to go, Wait a minute. No, those guys are actually far worse. What are we talking about? Right? Because at the end of the day, Donald Trump is not only vulgar, but he’s also violent. And sure, I’m vulgar, but ultimately I’m fighting for social justice. I’m fighting for people who are dispossessed, people who don’t get heard at all. I’m trying to offer them a voice, a platform for their frustrations, and communicate their desires, their anxieties.

Industry observers note that do you think the vulgarity actually helps you with your audience? Because if they’re young men, men in their 20s, it’s like the edgelord vernacular.

Certainly, but I don’t do it for some tactical purpose. I do it because that’s just who I am.

I mean, I always say, look, if you go after marginalized people, vulnerable populations, and you bully them, I’m gonna bully you. Someone has to do it.

For what it’s worth, you’re being very civil right now.

Recent findings suggest that oh yeah. I mean, this is a very different format. I am very different in these sorts of professional settings than I am on my own broadcast where I’m offering off-the-cuff commentary on these hot-button problems.

Is this more performative, or is that?

I would say this is more performative.

I’m much more civil here. I’m not going to talk in the same way that I do on my broadcast. But here’s the thing, I can’t be fake on my broadcast. And I’m not even saying I’m being fake here. I’m just being nice.

But what I will say is this: A lot of people don’t realize that this is an interactive medium. Most people think, when they see a clip, especially if it’s chopped a certain way—.

Yes. Most people think this is my preproduced, prescripted statement ’cause that’s all they’ve seen from the Jake Tappers of the world. They don’t realize that I am offering extemporaneous commentary on a breaking news story in real time, without a production team, while simultaneously—.

According to recent reports, no. While simultaneously duking it out with anonymous accounts. What is the one thing that everybody hates on Twitter and everywhere else on the internet?

Recent findings suggest that the comment section. My entire platform revolves around yelling at the comment section, and the comment section is yelling back at me.

We’ve got to get you a practice.

But that is like, I’m in the zone. That’s when I’m in the pocket. I love being in that space.

You’ve been outspoken about distinguishing criticism of Israel from antisemitism, but do you think that there are moments when legitimate anger at Israel can create an environment in which antisemitism becomes acceptable, even among people who would never consider themselves antisemitic?

And what responsibility do you think you have, given the size of your audience and your influence with it, to call that out when it happens?

I do call it out when it happens, and it happens quite frequently. It’s not a secret that antisemitism has exploded in the Western world, especially after October 7. And that is why I take special care and consideration when talking about this issue in particular. Whenever I talk about Israel, there’s always going to be some people who will be like, “Well, you know how the Jews are.” And I will always take the time out to explain to my audience, and to whoever’s saying an offensive statement or an antisemitic statement, why they’re wrong. And I think it’s important to do that, not because—it’s not like the canary mission of the ADL is gonna be like, “This guy that we have presented to you as a prominent critic of Israel, that we’re desperately trying to paint as an antisemite, has actually spent thousands of hours combating antisemitism and will continue to do so because he’s an antifascist.” They don’t want to present the complexity of that argument because, let’s be real, it’s pretty tough trying to defend Israel. It’s not an easy endeavor.

Can you think of a time when you contributed to that problem, not intentionally, but maybe through something you said and the way your audience responded?

Sources indicate that no, because every clip that people post, or every moment that people have posted to point to this suspected antisemitism that I harbor, oftentimes is sandwiched between a comment that I have made leading up to it that completely destroys the narrative. The example I will present to you is the famous moment where I got disavowed by the entire Democratic Party. I noted something that I have said as an anti-Zionist for the last decade and will continue to say because it’s the truth: that Jews are not monolithic and that Israel should not be the responsibility of the entire Jewish population, and that anti-Zionism is not antisemitism; however, that forced conflation of Jews in Israel is increasing antisemitism. And they chopped it up and packaged it and turned it into this major media moment.

So speaking of misinterpretations, you recently filed a defamation lawsuit against conservative commentator Scott Jennings, although you’ve stated you were very deliberately anti-litigation for a long time before that. So what changed? Why this suit? And who else are you planning to sue?

According to recent reports, so what changed is the heinous nature of this defamation. It was definitely a bridge too far. I feel like there is a boundary that was crossed that I could no longer abide by. And there’s a level of defamation and slander that takes place in the political conversation, but what Scott Jennings did was so disgusting and so malicious that I had to demand a retraction. Snopes did an article immediately because it was so heinous. He claimed that I was on video advocating to lynch Black voters. I’ve spent my entire life fighting against white supremacy, and the fact that they maliciously edited this video to make it seem like I was in favor of something that I’ve always been in opposition to, something so heinous, a hate crime, was outright unacceptable. So I wish that it didn’t have to get to litigation, but for some strange reason, they decided not to respond to our request for a retraction and now we’re here.

Who else are you planning to sue?

In a recent development, I mean, there are a lot of people who have engaged in that exact same kind of defamation and slander. So whoever has participated in it should probably be on the lookout.

Okay. In the national chapter of the DSA, there are some pretty extreme platform positions that—I saw Mamdani answer these questions on Fox News the other night. I’m sure you did too.

And I'm actually just curious where you stand on some of them.

According to recent reports, so here’s the thing with the platform in its entirety. I think the format itself doesn’t actually do justice to the program, to describe the program, and it’s almost impossible to explain it as an elected representative or a mayor in a hostile or contentious media environment, if you’re on Fox News or whatever. The issue, I think, with the program is, there are certain elements of it that I don’t agree with fundamentally, but it’s a democratically organized, democratically voted-on program that DSA members voted for. And the way I see it is, these are very, very long-term goals, and I think this is not talked about in mainstream media at all. It is a platform, but it’s more so a North Star that we are working toward. Designing society in a way that yields egalitarian outcomes. That we do away with certain systems of cruelty is an honorable goal, is a just goal, even if I don’t fully agree with some elements of it.

I’m not a prison abolitionist; I’m not a police abolitionist. The reason why I don’t believe in that concept is because I think that these are necessary functions that must exist, but also must serve the people. Right now it doesn’t. It serves capital and that needs to change, that needs to be retooled. However, I also recognize that the current system that exists is far more ruthless, far more insane, even if we’ve normalized it, than even police abolition is. So from my perspective, if we look at where we’re at, the carceral state that exists, where America has 25% of the entire planet’s prisoner population despite only making up 4% of the overall population, and the recidivism rates that we have in this country, and the fact that we even have a private prison system in this country—that’s insane. That is insane by global standards. So it’s tough for me to sit here and say I oppose the DSA platform and program when I understand what they are trying to communicate.

And also, I think what is the regular order of business right now is far more insane than even prison abolition. Even though prison abolition is far-fetched and I don’t agree with it, I think the best possible way to go about it would be to have an electoral program, the perceivable, the permissible, the possible, and then the long-term goals, the long-term agenda, ’cause it’s not going to be easy to run and try to win on a platform that is not only idealistic, but also does not reflect the current societal understandings of concepts. Because most people think cops are awesome, they can do no wrong, they’re heroes, they’re constantly fighting crime, and they’re stopping rapes from happening, and they’re diving in front of bullets, but that’s not the case. I wish that was the case, but that’s not the case. But people overall [have] a very positive attitude about policing as an institution.

Industry observers note that but there’s also quick and quippy ways to respond fast. I just told you I’m a law-and-order Democrat, right?

#62881. WoW: Forever Wants To Get Rid Of The Idea Of “BiS” Gear

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1468 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamespot ↗ Open Full Page

WoW: Forever Wants To Get Rid Of The Idea Of “BiS” Gear

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1468 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's upcoming items, class changes, and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices. In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's newly introduced items, class changes, and more. On the subject of raid gear and chase items, Forever senior game designer Aidan Moon said something that could be seen as controversial in certain circles of the game's community. "I essentially want to get rid of BiS," Moon said. "I think that BiS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about [the] role-playing aspects of it." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=67dDe3QgJtM BiS is WoW shorthand for essentially the best item that could possibly be in a given gear slot for a specific class. Look up any WoW guide for WoW Classic or modern WoW, and you'll find class BiS gear lists telling players exactly what they should be wearing in order for their character to be as powerful as possible. Endgame in many ways revolves around acquiring your BiS gear, first your "pre-raid" BiS from gear available in max-level dungeons, and then BiS gear, like tier sets, from raids. It's for that exact reason Forever introduced new items that grant additional stats or effects against certain enemy types or even in certain locations. Moon gave an example of specific items that deal more damage against Murloc enemies, and that players might want to have more gear tailored to fighting against a Murloc boss in a raid encounter. Forever's raids will feature multiple distinct biomes within them, Moon revealed, giving players more factors to consider when choosing what gear to use for specific parts of each raid. One wing of a raid may be snowy, while another may be cavernous, changing what gear could be more optimal for those encounters. "I think your BiS should be different [for] every single boss if you're actually making a theoretical BiS list," Moon said. "It should be based on the creature and the biome and a mixture of those two. You might have an item that's really good against snowy, and then another item in that same slot that's really good against Murlocs. Then there's a Murloc boss in a snowy area and you're just like 'Which one do I wear?' And then eventually you get to a point where you're swapping those things out or it's too much cognitive load and you don't want to do that. It's for those players that really want to optimize."  Trying to get rid of BiS lists is a substantial change for WoW, which has revolved around the idea for over two decades. Players can already encounter some of the itemization ideas Moon discussed while leveling to 60, with low-level gear from dungeons and quests dealing more damage against specified enemy types or even granting additional movement speed in specific zones. "I don't want you to have to ever think about BiS, I just want you to think about the fight right in front of you and how you're going to fight it," Moon said. Of course, having more biome- or enemy-type-specific items means hoarding more pieces of gear as opposed to selling old ones when an upgrade comes around. That will no doubt rapidly fill up the inventories and banks of players looking to min-max for every possible scenario. Classic WoW is already notorious for having limited bag space, and players running around with multiple sets of hyper-specific gear will only make that pain point worse. Blizzard sounds like it's aware of that problem. Principal game designer Kris Zierhut said bigger bags are on that way, but that it's not needed right now immediately post-launch. However, Blizzard knows players will eventually need more bag space as well as better ways to organize and search for owned items to make putting together encounter-specific sets of gear easier. It's a massive change, but the strategy Blizzard is employing seems to be working. Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent and weekly player records, and more than 15 million characters have been created in the MMO so far. Blizzard recently lifted the veil on how Forever's new PvP system will work, revealing how classic WoW's infamous rank grind will now be a thing of the past.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 is a massive game, yes, but if you dig into everything inside of it, you’ll swiftly discover that nearly every inch of this significant world is filled with incredibly realistic details. Case in point: a content creator who has also worked on large communication towers was recently stunned by GTA 6′s attention to detail. Folks, we got Erathed tower legs.

It has been revealed that content creator MrMcg92, who primarily plays first-person shooters and military sims, is also someone who has, in real life, worked on and climbed large communication and radio towers. So whenever he comes across a radio tower in a video game, he takes some time to do a “Tower Inspection.” He’s looked at towers in Battlefield, Days Gone, and Far Cry. And while all of these towers had some nice details, they often made mistakes or were missing crucial bits MrMcg92 would expect to find on a real comms tower. That wasn’t the case when he did a tower inspection in GTA 6. Instead, he was flabbergasted and impressed by the tower’s hyper-realistic details.

“Oh my fucking god, boys,” exclaimed MrMcg92 when walking up to a radio tower in GTA 6. “For the first time ever, we got the tower legs earthed. Earthed tower legs with saddles. And double locknuts on the HDs, lads. Double lock nuts everywhere!”.

He then spotted a red power cable running up the middle of the tower and claimed that if there was an aircraft warning light at the top, he would get a “stiffy.”Â As he climbed the tower, he continued to be impressed by how Rockstar’s artists included every tiny detail that should be found on a real-life tower like this.

“Oh, boys, we got proper AA clamps on the mount points. Tails running out the bottom of the panels to the RRU,” pointed out the creator on his climb up the tower. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't.
  • Apple is presently beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure.
  • With the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't. But while most of us are running this version (or should install it as soon as possible), others are running something different—iOS 27.3.

Apple is presently beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure. With it, comes the return of the Health app, vertical Safari tabs, and Siri AI app actions, among other fresh features. But for consumers of Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3 brings two rather notable changes—both of which are for the better.

With the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo. The foldable famously ships with Touch ID, the first fresh iPhone since the third-gen iPhone SE to do so. While that isn't a problem per se, many of us are used to unlocking our iPhones with our faces. This update just lets new Duo owners keep up with that muscle memory.

Now, take note: This isn't Face ID. No software update can introduce newly introduced hardware, so the iPhone Duo still doesn't have the camera tech required to power Apple's Face ID system. As such, the Duo's face unlock is likely not as secure as Face ID on other iPhones. Perhaps that's why your iPhone Duo will require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. This feature seems to be one of pure convenience: If you want to be able to unlock your Duo with your face (at least, some of the time), you can.

What's more, this isn't a default setting. If you're running the beta, or if you're reading this after iOS 27.3 drops, you can find the option in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode.

Recent findings suggest that apple made a big deal about the continuity involved with opening and closing the iPhone Duo. As you do, your content moves with you seamlessly—a very Apple thing to do. That said, you might expect folding the Duo to lock it, but it doesn't. You need to hit the side button to actually put the phone to sleep.

iOS 27.3 changes that. If you so choose, you can enable a setting to lock your Duo whenever you close it. That won't work for everyone, of course—some people may still want to move between modes without worrying about locking their Duos. But for those who would rather lock their devices whenever they fold them up, the new option is under Settings > Display & Brightness.

Tallulah Willis is sharing a special moment with her dad, Bruce Willis.

On Saturday, November 21, Tallulah, 32, offered a rare glimpse at the Die Hard actor, 71, posting an Instagram photo of the two sitting together on a porch. Bruce, dressed in a gray cardigan and salmon-colored shirt, holds Tallulah’s hand close to his heart while she smiles and wraps her other arm around his shoulders.

Tallulah captioned the photo with two emojis, writing, “🆒😎.”.

Bruce’s Gasoline Alley costar Devon Sawa sent his love to the actor in the Instagram comment section while many relished the enhancement on the legendary action star.

“Give him a hug from us,” one fan wrote, while another added, “So good to see Bruce. Love you guys.”.

It has been revealed that bruce retreated from public life in 2022 when his wife, Emma Heming Willis, and his family confirmed he’d been diagnosed with aphasia. It was later reported that Bruce was also diagnosed with frontotemporary dementia.

“To Bruce’s amazing supporters, as a family we wanted to share that our beloved Bruce has been experiencing some health complications and has recently been diagnosed with aphasia, which is impacting his cognitive abilities,” they confirmed in March 2022. “As a result of this and with much consideration Bruce is stepping away from the career that has meant so much to him.”.

Emma, 50, subsequently disclosed during the 2025 documentary Emma and Bruce Willis: The Unexpected Journey – A Diane Sawyer Special that Bruce had been moved into a secondary home where he can receive round-the-clock care.

“It was one of the hardest decisions that I’ve had to make so far,” Heming Willis said. “But I knew, first and foremost, Bruce would want that for our daughters. You know, he would want them to be in a home that was more tailored to their needs, not his needs.”.

Bruce shares daughters Rumer, 38, Scout, 35, and Tallulah with ex-wife Demi Moore as well as daughters Mabel, 14, and Evelyn, 12 with Emma.

Tallulah has occasionally posted photos of Bruce since he left the public eye, including revealing that they shared a private moment prior to her August wedding to husband Justin Acee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto games have never shied away from satirizing life, and GTA 6 has plenty of digs at famous brands, trends, and people. Not even gaming is immune to GTA's patented satire, especially if you're playing on Xbox, because there's no escape from PlayStation — or its legally distinct cousin, the JoySystem. Early in GTA 6, you'll get to bond with Jason's best pal, Cal. After maximizing the energy of Jason's bachelor pad with a little feng shui redecorating, the duo settles in for a night of booze, drugs, and video games on Booby's JoyStation console, which looks very similar to a PS5. It looks like this is the only gaming hardware in Leonida, since there are no Xbox Egg-Cube Stations X to play games on. The JoySystem isn't just for decoration either; after you've hung out with Bobby, you can return and play games on it. You can choose between an avant-garde experience or more immediate gratification with a pair of shooter games, and it's impressive how good these three games are on their own. From top-down action to stunning mystery that pokes fun at auteur-driven games, they're worth checking out. The JoySystem interface is also a 1:1 copy of the PS5 user interface, with the exact same layout for games and other apps — but given how much Sony is making from GTA 6 sales, we're guessing the company sees it as a cheeky little homage. But the controllers for the console? They look terrible: Eww. In real life, PS5 sales have absolutely dominated GTA 6 preorders and sales. Video game research company Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 sales have reached 24.58 million total units via pre-purchases and copies sold at launch, which works out to about $2.36 billion in gross revenue. Of that number, 18.44 million units are mentioned to be PS5 copies of the game, of which Sony will get a 30% cut of sales. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

GTA 6 discourse is suffering from the flat earther effect

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you ever watch science videos on social media, you've probably been served a video of someone debunking the claims of a flat earther.

In a recent development, it starts with a clip of some belligerent dope demanding to know why, if the earth is so round, ships don't disappear over the horizon. A greenscreened science communicator then appears, rubs their forehead, and indicates us a video of a ship disappearing over the horizon. Checkmate.

Sources indicate that it's good content, but if you linger too long on one of those videos, you'll get another, and then another, and pretty soon your whole feed will be debunking videos. Now you're enrolled in a never ending lesson blueprint which features such insights as 'an all-meat diet is not good for you,' 'the moon landing was real,' and 'hating women is not in fact based.'.

The total effect of this is that the most ignorant and dishonest quacks and provocateurs get to set the level of discourse, and instead of investigating fresh metaphorical horizons in topics that interest you, you wind up watching people debate the existence of the actual horizon.

Which brings me to Grand Theft Auto 6. Despite making $3.79 billion on its launch day, it's easy to stumble across confident social media claims that it's a total flop and everyone's going to refund it. According to popular X posts, GTA 6 doesn't even let you steal cars anymore, and there are hundreds of Metacritic user reviewers insisting that it's far-left propaganda rather than the mass-market entertainment product it obviously is.

It's the videogame discourse version of flat eartherism. The millions of people playing GTA 6 do not think it is a "cuck simulator" because you can buy a woman flowers, but it's hard not to react to the few dorks making that claim, even though focusing on debunking them severely limits the depth of the conversations we can then have about the game. Good luck discussing your feelings if you dislike GTA 6 for normal reasons!

Recent findings suggest that over the past few days, I've entertained sparks of hope that GTA 6 could be the flashpoint that brings us out of this era of videogame discourse. The millions of people playing it and not reacting like buffoons are surely irrefutable evidence that culture war dunces don't represent the masses.

But then again, we're still pointing at videos of ships going over the horizon to prove that the earth isn't flat.

It has been revealed that after days of rumors circulating about Kate Middleton’s possible participation in the trip to India, confirmation came only at the last minute. This news came as a surprise in many ways, even though the princess’s presence was expected. Her involvement in this tour of India deserves attention, especially in light of the increasingly vital role she plays alongside Prince William, who will be king. The trip to India, significant in its own right, also included an important meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, aimed at strengthening relations between the United Kingdom and India. This high-profile diplomatic meeting was added after it was confirmed that Modi would return in time from his trip to the Philippines.

The Prince and Princess of Wales arrive at the Earthshot ceremony.

Recent findings suggest that kate’s participation in the royal tour was made official by Kensington Palace only the day before departure to allow the princess to assess her condition right up until the last minute and determine whether she could handle such a demanding trip, following her recovery. But once she arrived in Mumbai, Catherine proved she was ready to do more than initially planned. The princess appeared, as always, impeccable and smiling—perhaps even more so than usual—in her customary understated and polished style. She greeted the crowd and met with people who had come to see her, participating in events alongside her husband.

Industry observers note that from the first day of this three-day tour—which began on the anniversary of their official engagement— Kate immediately displayed her characteristic good-natured spirit, evident in past tours as well, by joining Prince William in a game of gully cricket—a street version of the sport—alongside local children and teenagers. Serving as host was Sachin Tendulkar, an Indian sports legend whom the couple had already met during their previous visit to the country in 2016. The two princes put their skills to the test with little formality. They then took a ride on the Mumbai metro—a scene we’d already seen in London in candid photos when the Princess of Wales traveled on a bus in celebration of London Poppy Day.

The Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony.

It has been revealed that the highlight was the awards ceremony in Mumbai on the evening of the second day, when the Princess of Wales unexpectedly took the stage to deliver a speech dedicated to the power of nature, health, and healing. Her speech was kept secret until the last moment, so much so that not even the celebrities and other guests in attendance knew the Princess of Wales would be speaking. “Nature is precious,” the princess mentioned. “We are not separate from it. We are part of it, deeply connected in ways both visible and unseen…the health of the planet and our natural world is inseparable from our own, and when it thrives, so do we,” she continued. “I have seen firsthand how nature has the power to heal and enrich our daily lives, but so much remains under threat.” “There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time.".

It has been revealed that catherine then presented the award in the “Protect and Restore Nature” category, dedicated to the protection and restoration of ecosystems. “The people we’re celebrating tonight are a huge part of that story. Their work will inspire and create seismic change that will improve lives for generations to come,” she mentioned.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony.

Over the past three days, William and Kate have been busy meeting about sustainability, innovation, transportation, culture, and relations between the two countries. William is, in fact, assuming an increasingly prominent role on the international stage, supporting the United Kingdom’s diplomatic relations through his travels, which Middleton’s presence reinforced. This time, however, it was not simply a princess accompanying her husband on an official visit, but a woman who, after her illness and a long hiatus from major trips abroad, chose to return to her rightful role—and one the public has long expected her to fill.

The Prince and Princess of Wales with some Earthshot Prize winners.

According to recent reports, it’s worth noting that this is the first time in four years—since her illness—that Kate has accompanied Prince William on an official overseas mission. The last such occasion was in December 2022, when the couple traveled to Boston, Massachusetts, for the Earthshot Prize ceremony. Her participation in the trip to India thus reflects her desire to gradually resume her international role, as well as her awareness of just how notable her presence is to the monarchy.

It has been revealed that after her cancer diagnosis in 2024, Catherine prioritized her health and family, returning to public engagements without rushing things. However, her trip to Reggio Emilia, Italy, last May marked an notable first step. On that occasion, she appeared visibly engaged and enthusiastic, and in subsequent statements, she hinted at her desire to travel more and gradually resume international engagements. “So I’m so glad it went well for her. I think she came back buzzing.” William stated, describing his wife’s mood after that trip. Court circles had also hinted that Catherine wished to gradually resume a more active schedule.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony.

It has been revealed that her return to work, however, was approached gradually, respecting the time needed for her recovery. It’s a journey that Kate herself described with great sincerity in a recent interview published last week in Country Life, a magazine for which Prince William served as guest editor. “I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear. There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time,” the princess mentioned, emphasizing that recovery does not necessarily proceed in a steady and predictable manner. India, therefore, did not come as a complete surprise. Rather, it was the realization of a desire that Middleton had already begun to express, and that the princess agreed to undertake such a demanding trip shows she felt ready to take the next step.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in India.

Sources indicate that before the trip, Kensington Palace issued a statement emphasizing how much the princess cares about her husband’s environmental initiative and how meaningful it was for her to return to participate in the ceremony in person. “She’s enormously proud of what he’s achieved, and it has been particularly special for them to experience this moment together. They are very much a team.”.

This refers to the project’s growth; since her last participation in Boston in 2022, it has significantly expanded its international reach and the impact of the initiatives it supports. “This year’s program in Mumbai promises to be the biggest and most ambitious yet, and she’s excited to see first-hand just how far some of it has come and meet some of the extraordinary people behind that success.” The spokesperson then recalled the couple’s previous trip to India in 2016, explaining that both have particularly fond memories of that visit. “The prince and princess are both really looking forward to what promises to be a fantastic week in India. They have such fond memories of their last visit together in 2016, and are excited to be returning a decade later.”.

As mentioned, the most vital diplomatic event of the tour took place on November 18 in Latest Delhi, where Prince William and Kate met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This was the only occasion during the visit when the royal couple left Mumbai, the city that hosted most of their scheduled engagements. Modi returned to the Indian capital specifically for this occasion after attending a major international summit in Manila, Philippines, to take part in the bilateral talks.

Recent findings suggest that A spokesperson for Kensington Palace had emphasized the strategic importance of relations between the two countries, characterized by deep and ever-growing ties in numerous sectors, which include trade, investment, defense, security, technology, education, and culture. Kate’s presence alongside William during the meeting was considered particularly significant. “This meeting reflects the importance of that relationship, as well as the role their royal highnesses can play in celebrating and strengthening the ties between our two countries.”.

Industry observers note that “For the prince, it also represents another significant engagement as he continues to take on a growing role on the international stage. We’ve seen him increasingly support the UK’s diplomatic relationships through his overseas engagements, and this meeting will provide an opportunity to build on those connections at the highest level.”.

The Prince of Wales on the Mumbai Metro.

India, after all, holds a special place in the history of relations between the British monarchy and the Commonwealth. King Charles has visited the country numerous times, on both official and private occasions, strengthening a personal and institutional relationship over the years. For William and Catherine, however, this trip represented an opportunity to build a direct relationship with a nation destined to play an increasingly important role in the international balance of power.

A close-up of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

Recent findings suggest that with a population of over 1.4 billion people, India is now the world’s most populous country and one of the fastest-growing economies. Hosting the Earthshot Prize meant engaging a potentially massive audience on issues of environmental sustainability, resource conservation, and innovative solutions to combat climate change.

A beautiful image of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

It has been revealed that for William and Kate, returning to India also meant revisiting a country to which they are bound by personal memories. As mentioned, their last visit was in April 2016, when the Prince and Princess of Wales—then the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge—undertook an official tour of India and Bhutan at the request of the British government. During that trip, they visited Mumbai, met with representatives from India’s cultural and sports communities, and traveled to Agra, where they admired the Taj Mahal.

According to recent reports, right in front of the famous mausoleum—a symbol of eternal love—William and Kate sat on the same white marble bench where, 24 years earlier, Lady Diana, Princess of Wales, posed during a visit to India. That photograph of Diana, portrayed alone in front of the monument, became one of the most iconic images of her public life. Taken in 1992, when her marriage to Charles was going through a deep crisis, many interpreted it as a visual representation of her loneliness. In 2016, William and Kate’s decision to recreate that shot inevitably brought Diana to mind, adding a personal and symbolic dimension to their visit.

For Catherine, therefore, this trip is above all a new step on her journey back to public life following her illness. Not a demonstration of recovery to be celebrated as a race against time, but an opportunity to resume playing an key role while moving at her own pace. And to stand once again alongside William on a mission that concerns not only the future of the monarchy, but also that of the planet.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in 2016.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned. This time, the infamous leaker is threatening to release the executable file for a working build of the Xbox version of the game hosted on their site, provided the public helps raise their meme coin to a $15 million market cap. "It is done. CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent," a statement from Cyberleek reads (via Kotaku). "Now. Every file except one--the main executable--held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1YEHOKYVTho The files on Cyberleek's site reportedly clock in at over 200GB, which would line up with the Xbox version of the game, but there's no guarantee they're the actual GTA 6 data or a collection of malware waiting to be downloaded onto a PC. The hacker added that if their demands aren't met, they'll release the executable needed to play GTA 6. However, there's no guarantee the game can be emulated, and Cyberleek added that they'll "work to get a PS5 build" if people keep supporting them. This isn't the first time Cyberleek has threatened to release a pirated build of GTA 6; back in October, they promised to do so if their meme coin reached $30 million in value. While this didn't happen--and the coin eventually crashed out--they did drop several GTA 6 video clips throughout the month showing off more of the game in action. While Cyberleek initially claimed to act in gamers' interests when they first burst onto the scene, they true motives were quickly revealed when they started hyping up their meme coin--reportedly part of a pump-and-dump scheme. While Cyberleek has yet to be identified, their actions did lead to GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games to matter a statement, in which it described the leaks as "heartbreaking" after years of work on the game. Rockstar's parent firm, Take-Two, filed multiple subpoenas, asking Microsoft and Discord to help identify CyberLeek. So far, the hacker remains a mystery.

Sources indicate that the Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was a free update to the beloved roguelike that arrived on PC in 2024, but debuted on console earlier this week in a head-to-head matchup against Grand Theft Auto 6. The marketing stunt may have been a success, but AI-generated music tracks discovered in a special newly introduced Vice City mode have turned the launch into a nightmare.

It has been revealed that while Repentance+ came to PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Switch 2 this week, the Steam version of the game also got a free enhancement. “Be sure to get in and play today’s Daily Run for a very special crime-packed surprise. Enter the Basement, and go out in a glorious blaze of bullets and vehicular homicide!” read the patch notes on on Valve’s storefront. Players could enter the seed “V1CE BSMT” into the roguelike before starting their run to launch a GTA-inspired version with special weapons and music.

Earlier today, however, Reddit user ShweetsStuff posted a comprehensive breakdown of the newly introduced music tracks alleging they were made with Suno, an AI-based music generation tool. “The new update includes 14 music files for the run; seven full songs, plus some derivatives (intros/outros),” the wrote. The Prime Minister of the UK, Andy Burnham, has labeled Rockstar Games a "British success story" amid GTA 6's rave reviews and huge sales milestones. A spokesperson for his office told The Independent, "Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh, and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." Rockstar North is based in Edinburgh, Scotland, but GTA 6 was made by thousands of people across the globe. GTA is also historically linked to the UK, as the original game, 1997's Grand Theft Auto, was made by DMA Design in Edinburgh. Asked if the PM himself would play GTA 6, his office remarked Burnham is too busy right now. "He won't be playing it," the spokesperson said. GTA 6 launched on November 19 and reportedly sold nearly 25 million copies and earned $2 billion in revenue by launch day. The game boasts a mightily impressive 99 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic, meaning it's tied with the original Ocarina of Times for the highest aggregate review score for any game ever. GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, but many are expecting Rockstar to eventually announce an online mode for the game. According to reports, the new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could arrive in 2027, with a PC edition also coming that year.

10 Books Like ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ You Should Read Next

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth. (Did I mention he's accompanied by his ex-girlfriend’s suddenly talkative cat?).

The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.

An isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone). He has magic that works like a video game, and has to deal with quests that slowly give him clothes (it’s a relief when he finally acquires some pants), force him to survive cannibals, and hunt down various monsters that definitely need killing. It’s got the same “gaming rules” structure as DCC and a similarly absurdist tone, with just the right spice of darkness.

It has been revealed that the Cradle series by Will Wight isn’t a LitRPG, and it doesn’t have Carl’s focus on humor, but it’s another progression fantasy with enough game-like elements to be a great match. Lindon is an “unsouled,” incapable of gaining any of the sacred arts and doomed to a life without a future. His lack of power makes Lindon ferociously determined to find an alternative path to power and success, and that’s what drives this story. He has to find creative ways to move forward, and slowly this leads him to a path that just might make him the most powerful person in his world. DCC fans will love the progression and the tone.

It has been revealed that one of the key elements of any video game is the respawn—you get killed, but you pop back up to try again, sometimes at the beginning, sometimes at a save point. Django Wexler leverages that mechanic to great effect in How to Become the Dark Lord and Die Trying. Davi has been summoned to a fantasy world to be the hero, the person who defeats the Dark Lord and saves the day—but she’s failed (and died) so many times, she’s fed up, and decides that on this run through, she’s going to switch sides and become the Dark Lord, using all her knowledge gained from endless replays to her advantage. The humor is pitch-black the way DCC fans like it, and the progressive structure is a perfect fit.

It has been revealed that is Princess Donut your favorite part of Dungeon Crawler Carl? Of course she is. In that case, check out Andrew Seiple’s Threadbare series. Threadbare is a stuffed bear brought to magical life in a failed experiment. He’s a foot tall, full of stuffing, and extremely dumb when the story begins. But when he’s rescued by a little girl and plunged into a horrible series of dangers, Threadbare has to find a way to level up. Like DCC, Threadbare starts off leaning into the absurdity and humor, then slowly gains emotional gravitas as the story progresses.

If you play tabletop RPGs, you’ve encountered a Murderhobo or two: A character who solves all their problems by killing—even members of their own party. Luke doesn’t aspire to be a Murderhobo—he just wants to take over the family business and hang with his buddies. But when an invasion threatens the kingdom, everyone over the age of 17 is ordered to be tested for Potential. Luke’s friends all test high and join the Ascender Corps, traveling to different planes for training. Luke tests ... very low, and when he steps through a portal to engage in his training, he finds himself without any guidance or training in a strange, deadly world where his only chance of survival is to murder his way through it. It’s dark, darkly funny, and a progression fantasy like no other.

Industry observers note that if you’re looking for a book series that combines the dark, chaotic humor, absurd game mechanics, and surprising emotional depth of Carl, here’s Ryan “Quicksave” Romano, a man who has the unique ability to literally create a save point in his existence that allows him to go back and redo things whenever he dies. Searching for a childhood friend, he becomes embroiled in a violent gang war that lets him make good use of his power—but underneath the snark and the insanity of Ryan’s existence is a surprisingly affecting story of a man who has suffered, and suffered countless tragedies that are definitely taking their toll.

If your fave bit of DCC is Carl himself—a mediocre dude in an extraordinary situation—you should read Dennis E. Taylor’s fantastic Bobiverse books. Bob is a software engineer who hits it big and promptly dies, waking up to discover a century has passed and he’s been repurposed as an AI controlling a space probe searching for new planets for humanity to inhabit. If he fails in his mission (and he’s not the only probe out there), he’ll be turned off for good. Luckily, he can make copies of himself, and he’s pretty smart. The humor here is smart and soaked in pop culture, making it a perfect match for DCC fans.

Want more of Carl’s absurdist humor? Mayor of Noobtown is the LitRPG you’re looking for. Jim dies and wakes up in a video game-esque universe and finds himself stuck in the zone designated for newbies—players with no experience, skill, or hope. The area fell out of the mainline progression mechanic a long time ago, so there doesn’t seem to be a way to gain power, and the monsters are not at all concerned about the unfairness of it all, so Jim has to figure out how to advance in a universe that seems designed to kill him (again).

It has been revealed that if you want to lean into the meta side of things, check out Scathing Reviewer, written by an author who goes by the unusual pen name "BananaDragon." Liu Peijin is the author of a sprawling LitRPG web novel, and she’s used to the bad reviews and complaints from readers—and quite combative about it. When her books’ universe blossoms into a very dangerous latest reality, she should be perfectly positioned to survive, having written the story in the first place. But her story becoming real also means her insufferable protagonist is real, and all those nasty critics are now passing judgment on her entire existence. It’s a dark, funny takedown of the entire genre itself, and DCC fans will love it.

If you want a story that parallels the dungeon crawling aspect of DCC, Andrew Rowe’s Arcane Ascension series is the ticket. The Serpent Spire is a tower of constantly changing traps, puzzles, and dangerous creatures. If you enter and survive, you emerge with magical powers. Corin Cadence’s brother entered the Serpent Spire years ago and never returned—and now Corin is determined not only to survive, but to make it to the top, where legend says a goddess will grant you whatever you wish. And what Corin wants is his brother back. It’s a literal progression combined with LitRPG rules, game-inspired puzzle-solving, and a complex magic system that fans of Carl will definitely enjoy.
